AI CLI Tools Community Digest 2026-11-12

Generated: 2026-11-12 02:12 UTC | Tools covered: 7

  • Claude Code
  • OpenAI Codex
  • Gemini CLI
  • GitHub Copilot CLI
  • OpenCode
  • Pi
  • Qwen Code
  • Claude Code Skills

Cross-Tool Comparison

Cross-Tool Comparison Report: AI CLI Ecosystem

Date: 2026-11-12 | Sources: 7 community digests (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Qwen Code)

1. Ecosystem Overview

The AI CLI tooling landscape has entered a hardening-and-parity phase: releases are increasingly incremental (point/alpha bumps, PTY daemon patches) while community energy concentrates on reliability, permissions, and multi-agent coordination rather than headline features. Across all seven trackers, trust-eroding bugs dominate: silent subagent failures, config that doesn't take effect at runtime, and permission classifiers that over-block legitimate work recur in every community. A clear Windows and ARM64/Linux-6.12 pain cluster appears in Codex, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, and Pi, suggesting platform QA debt industry-wide. Simultaneously, an emerging cross-harness ecosystem layer is visible — MCP event buses, hook-based policy gates, shared coordination servers (Concord), and patch-preservation tools — signaling that developers now run multiple agents concurrently and need infrastructure between them. Meanwhile, Qwen Code's 1.0 Preview and OpenCode's v2 rollout show the OSS challengers consolidating toward production-grade agent architectures.

2. Activity Comparison

Tool Issues (updated 24h) PRs (updated 24h) Discussions Releases (24h) Release Status
Claude Code ~50 reported; 10 shown 1 (closed, unmerged) N/A (none provided) 0 No release; entitlement bug churn
OpenAI Codex 10+ shown (heavy activity) 10+ (all copyberry[bot], batch-hardening) Yes — Ideas, Q&A, Show-and-tell active 7 (1 substantive + 6 alpha) Fast-moving alpha pipeline
Gemini CLI 10+ shown (~30 updated) 10+ shown (~20 updated) N/A (none provided) 0 No release; PR-heavy week
GitHub Copilot CLI 41 updated (30 shown) 0 N/A 2 (prerelease) Incremental quality fixes
OpenCode ~50 updated 10+ (feature-heavy) N/A (none provided) 1 (process-daemon-v0.5.2) v2 rollout in progress
Pi 50 updated 23 updated Yes — Show-and-tell (Concord integration) 0 No release; subsystem maturation
Qwen Code 10+ shown (CI-dominated) 10+ (architectural) N/A (none provided) 1 (v1.0.0-preview) Major preview launch

Notes:

  • Claude Code, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, and Qwen Code had no Discussions data provided in the source digests. These are marked "N/A" rather than "inactive" — absence of reported data is not evidence of an empty channel.
  • OpenAI Codex and Pi are the only tools with confirmed active Discussions in this snapshot; Codex's Show-and-tell is the single richest source of ecosystem-level innovation (see §3).
  • Codex's PR count is inflated by copyberry[bot] automated fixes — a coordination signal (hardening push) more than a contributor-count signal.
  • Qwen Code's issue activity is dominated by CI bot churn (#14724 at 325 comments), so raw counts overstate human engagement.

3. Shared Feature Directions

The following requirements appear across three or more communities, indicating genuine ecosystem-level demand:

3.1 Multi-Agent Coordination & Guardrails

  • Codex (Show-and-tell: claude-bulkhead, Concord, Pushary, TreeHarbor), Pi (Concord integration discussion #12063), OpenCode (subagent concurrency cap #63227), Gemini CLI (parallel/shared-memory subagents #18287), Qwen Code (workflow agent permission reliability #16425).
  • Need: shared work-state across harnesses, file-claim coordination, hook-based policy gates, and bounded subagent concurrency to prevent runaway cost and agents killing each other's processes.

3.2 Config Honored at Runtime

  • Claude Code (autocompact override persists, #108987; settings.json restarts), OpenCode (default_agent silently reverts, #62002; 5s vs 30s MCP timeout doc drift, #63092), Gemini CLI (browser agent ignores settings.json, #22267), Qwen Code (docs say restart needed, hot-reload works, #16925).
  • Need: live config application and consistency between discovery/registration layers and execution layers.

3.3 Permission / Safety Classifier False Positives

  • Claude Code (Cowork email blocks #98287; desktop MCP refusals #108921; repeated "false positive" reports), Codex (auto-review scope over-retention #58422), Copilot CLI (HTTP 422 cybersecurity flags on flaky-test debugging #5335), Qwen Code (Read deny rules leak through grep/glob #16653).
  • Need: precise, auditable permission scopes with review paths — not blanket over-blocking of owner-authorized actions.

3.4 Remote / SSH / Headless Automation

  • Codex (scheduled tasks over SSH #34946, auto-connect #59931), Claude Code (cloud scheduled tasks #98287), Gemini CLI (headless-mode suspension anxiety #20813; /skill-name in non-interactive mode #29546), Qwen Code (Managed Agent parity: web terminal, client filesystems, durable /loop).
  • Need: first-class non-interactive execution for CI/scripted/remote use, with clear ToS and permission semantics.

3.5 Subagent Observability & Correctness

  • Gemini CLI (#22323 MAX_TURNS misreported as GOAL success; #21983 Wayland false success), Claude Code (silent failures theme), OpenCode (session history search #63411), Pi (queue_update for discarded injected input #10317), Qwen Code (verify-then-repair loop #16941).
  • Need: agents that accurately report their own failure/interruption state — currently the most trust-damaging bug class for power users.

3.6 Cost / Usage-Window Controls

  • Codex (5-hour vs weekly window choice, #60953/#60954), Claude Code (disable cash Usage Credits #92087; 1M context credit errors), OpenCode (subagent concurrency cap; OpenCode Go account auto-balancing #63354).
  • Need: user-selectable usage windows and predictable consumption.

3.7 Cross-Platform Polish (Windows / ARM64 / Wayland)

  • Codex (6 of top 10 issues Windows-tagged), Copilot CLI (WSL2 ARM64 clipboard #3534; aarch64 ENOEXEC #5424), Gemini CLI (Wayland #21983; PowerShell freeze #30247), Pi (Windows pi -p hang #12068), OpenCode (Windows install/upgrade friction).
  • Need: parity in sandboxing, install, and terminal handling outside macOS/Linux-x64.

4. Differentiation Analysis

Dimension Claude Code OpenAI Codex Gemini CLI Copilot CLI OpenCode Pi Qwen Code
Primary user Individual Pro + org devs; VS Code-centric ChatGPT Pro + enterprise; Windows-heavy Enterprise/security-conscious; Google Cloud-adjacent GitHub/Entra enterprise; accessibility-aware OSS power users; self-hosters Long-running autonomous agents; NixOS/CI OSS deployers; Qwen/Qoder accounts
Feature focus IDE integration, session/workspace UX, voice Windows sandbox hardening, GCP tool delivery, image models Agent/subagent subsystem, AST navigation, enterprise telemetry Permission control, MCP auth, session UX, a11y v2 desktop/TUI, plugin API parity, scheduling pi-durable persistence, extension lifecycle 1.0 agent loop, Managed Agent parity, Web Shell
Technical approach Tight VS Code coupling; hardcoded defaults (e.g. includeWorktrees: false) Bot-driven hardening; incremental GCP tool declarations Bash-native model affinity; ACP mode parity Prerelease cadence; ACP session-store Event-bus, MCP bus publishing, concurrency bounds Durable storage/replication, atomic enqueue APIs Event-bus agent loop, opt-in preview tracks
Community channel Issues (no Discussions reported) Issues + active Discussions Issues (no Discussions reported) Issues (no Discussions reported) Issues (no Discussions reported) Issues + Show-and-tell Issues (no Discussions reported)
Signature strength Ecosystem mindshare; org controls Release velocity (7/24h) AST/enterprise research direction Accessibility + Entra integration Plugin extensibility Durable state for indefinite runs Preview consolidation (Qoder + Qwen)

Key distinctions:

  • Claude Code optimizes for IDE-native workflows but suffers from hardcoded integration assumptions (worktrees, telemetry→plugin coupling).
  • Codex is the only tool shipping at a near-daily cadence, but its Windows surface is the industry's largest liability.
  • Gemini CLI is the only community pursuing AST-aware code navigation as a coherent multi-issue research direction — a longer-horizon bet on semantic tooling.
  • Copilot CLI differentiates on enterprise identity (Entra) and accessibility, but has zero PR activity this window.
  • OpenCode and Pi are the plugin/extension platforms — and their pain points (V2 composer parity, extension lifecycle receipts) reflect that they're being used as infrastructure, not just tools.
  • Qwen Code is the only tool launching a major version this window, betting on merging two agent lineages.

5. Community Momentum & Maturity

Highest raw activity:

  • OpenAI Codex — 7 releases/24h, bot-driven PR batch, active Discussions. Fastest iteration, but issue tracker is a Windows-reliability queue.
  • OpenCode — ~50 issues + feature-dense PRs (concurrency caps, MCP bus, session search). Strong momentum on v2.
  • Qwen Code — 1.0 Preview launch, event-bus refactor, Managed parity features. High architectural ambition, but CI signal-to-noise is poor.

Highest engagement quality:

  • Pi — 50 issues + 23 PRs, with a genuine Show-and-tell ecosystem (Concord integration). The only community where external developers are building cross-harness infrastructure on top of the tool.
  • Codex — Discussions produce novel ecosystem primitives (claude-bulkhead, Pushary, TreeHarbor) that address multi-agent problems no single vendor is solving.

Maturity indicators:

  • Claude Code — High issue volume but only 1 PR in 24h, closed unmerged. Suggests a gated contribution model; community energy is frustrated energy (entitlement lockouts, silent failures).
  • Gemini CLI — Steady, well-curated PR flow (ACP parity, env-var semantics, worktree persistence). Mature engineering process; less community-generated innovation.
  • Copilot CLI — 41 issues updated but zero PRs. Prerelease-only cadence with no visible external contribution path.
  • OpenCode — Long-standing bugs finally closing (#4283 clipboard after a year, 135 👍) — a sign of backlog reduction, but also of how long trust issues linger.

Momentum ranking (subjective, by iteration + ecosystem energy):

  1. OpenAI Codex (velocity)
  2. OpenCode (v2 feature depth)
  3. Pi (ecosystem/Show-and-tell)
  4. Qwen Code (architectural leap)
  5. Gemini CLI (steady)
  6. Claude Code (gated, frustration-heavy)
  7. Copilot CLI (prerelease-only, no PR path)

6. Trend Signals

For technical decision-makers:

  1. Multi-agent orchestration is becoming a first-class requirement, not a power-user hack. The emergence of Concord, claude-bulkhead, and TreeHarbor — all community-built, cross-harness — means your team will likely run Claude Code, Codex, and others simultaneously on one machine. Budget for resource isolation (process guards, port conflicts, file claims) and prefer tools with hook/MCP policy gates.

  2. "Silent failure" is the dominant trust risk. Every community reports agents that claim success while failing (Gemini CLI #22323, Codex #56951, Claude Code silent-failure theme, Pi's silent capability loss). If you're building automated pipelines, do not trust agent-reported status — add independent verification (Qwen Code's verify-then-repair #16941 is the right pattern).

  3. Windows is a second-class citizen across the board. Six of Codex's top 10 issues are Windows; Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi, and Gemini CLI all have Windows/ARM64 blockers. If your org is Windows-heavy, pilot on Linux/macOS first and track sandbox ACL regressions specifically.

  4. Permission classifiers are over-blocking legitimate work. Codex (422 cybersecurity flags), Claude Code (Cowork email blocks), and Copilot CLI all show safety systems firing on ordinary debugging. Plan for allowlist/escalation paths before deploying unattended automation.

  5. Config predictability is an underrated selection criterion. Tools with documented config-drift bugs (OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Claude Code) will cost you debugging time. Favor tools where settings changes take effect live and are verifiable — Qwen Code's hot-reload (despite doc drift) and OpenCode's auto-balancing flags are directional.

  6. Enterprise telemetry and abuse-system tension is unresolved. Gemini CLI's headless-mode suspension (#20813) and PR #30010's skill_name telemetry work show that headless/CI usage can trip abuse systems. Enterprises should validate ToS posture before scaling headless deployments.

  7. OSS challengers are consolidating. Qwen Code 1.0 and OpenCode v2 are converging on event-bus agent loops, durable sessions, and plugin APIs — the same architecture the incumbents already have. Expect feature parity within 2–3 quarters, with differentiation shifting to model quality, cost, and ecosystem.

For developers building on these tools:

  • Prioritize extension APIs with lifecycle receipts (Pi #10317, OpenCode #51209) — you'll need them for reliable automation.
  • Watch the MCP event bus (OpenCode #63261) and hook-based policy gates (Codex Show-and-tell) as the emerging integration standard.
  • Assume your users run multiple harnesses — build for portability via MCP and AGENTS.md conventions, not vendor-specific hooks.

Report compiled from 7 community digests dated 2026-11-12. All counts reflect snapshot values; Discussions marked "N/A" indicate no data provided, not inactive channels.

Per-Tool Reports

Claude Code — anthropics/claude-code

Claude Code Skills Highlights

Source: anthropics/skills

Claude Code Skills Community Highlights Report — 2026-11-12

1. Top Skills Ranking (by discussion activity)

The most-watched PRs in this dataset are all OPEN, and notably most have a Comments: undefined field — meaning the shown signal is attention/retention (creation → last update windows of up to 8 months) rather than raw comment counts. Ranked by visibility and update recency:

# Skill / Fix What it does Discussion Highlights Status Link
1 skill-creator: isolate trigger evals Fixes false triggget misses: per-worker command probes compete, select() on subprocess pipes fails on Windows, unrelated tools stop the scan Directly tied to Issue #1352 (parallel workers cross-matching UUIDs → near-zero trigger rates) and #556 (0% trigger rate) — the eval harness is the community's biggest pain point OPEN (since 2026-06-10, active to 2026-09-16) PR #1298
2 mcp-builder: mcp>=2 streamable_http_client Migrates to streamable_http_client + create_mcp_http_client for custom headers after the mcp>=2.0.0 rename Breaking-change fix tracked as #1668; blocks anyone building MCP servers on current SDKs OPEN (since 2026-09-08) PR #1742
3 webapp-testing: remove shell=True Replaces subprocess.Popen(..., shell=True) in with_server.py with safe command spawning Security hardening (CWE-78 command injection) — part of a cluster of webapp-testing fixes OPEN (since 2026-10-06) PR #1980
4 docx: LibreOffice timeout = error accept_changes.py returns Error on soffice timeout and verifies w:ins/w:del removal before claiming success Fixes silent-success failure mode in a core document skill OPEN (since 2026-09-19) PR #1792
5 notion-spec-to-implementation + quantitative-resume-auditor Turns Notion spec pages into implementable tasks with acceptance criteria; audits resumes quantitatively Two-in-one community skill bundle; long-lived (Jun–Oct) OPEN PR #1245
6 document-typography Quality control for AI-generated docs: orphan wraps, widow paragraphs, numbering misalignment Widely-scoped claim ("affects every document Claude generates"); early-staged OPEN (Mar 2026) PR #514
7 pyxel Retro game dev in Python: implementation, headless input-driven runs, frame inspection Longest-running active PR in the set (Mar → Nov 2026) OPEN PR #525
8 proofcore-contract-auditor Static analysis of Solidity/Rust contracts + Merkle audit proofs anchored to TON Web3 vertical; vendor-authored, fast follow-up OPEN PR #1771

2. Community Demand Trends (from Issues)

  • Trust & namespace security (top issue, 46 comments): #492 — community skills distributed under the anthropic/ namespace enable impersonation and trust-boundary abuse. This is the single loudest thread in the repo.
  • Enterprise/org workflow automation: #228 (17 👍8) — org-wide skill sharing without manual .skill file shuffling; #1143 (15 👍) — account email change to prevent workspace data loss.
  • Evaluation infrastructure reliability: #556 (13 comments) and #1352 — run_eval.py produces 0% / false-negative trigger rates, especially with parallel workers.
  • Context-budget discipline: #1487 — claude-api skill eagerly injects ~156k tokens, exhausting context in one tool call.
  • Memory/state compression: #1329 — symbolic-notation compact-memory for long-running agents.
  • Quality-gate pipelines: #1385 — three-gate calibration → adversarial review → delivery verification.
  • Plugin surface hygiene: #189 (👍9) — document-skills and example-skills ship identical content, causing duplicates.
  • Skill-authoring best practices: #202 — skill-creator reads like dev docs, not an operational skill; #2064 — descriptions state what but not when to use.

3. High-Potential Pending Skills

Active-comment/recently-updated PRs that could land soon:

  • PR #1245 — notion-spec-to-implementation + quantitative-resume-auditor (updated 2026-10-15)
  • PR #1980 — webapp-testing shell=True removal (updated 2026-11-01)
  • PR #1792 — docx timeout-as-error (updated 2026-11-01)
  • PR #2019 — xlsx worksheet-scoped defined names in external_links_at_risk (updated 2026-11-03, fixes #2013)
  • PR #1950 — claude-api Python pause_turn runner guidance (updated 2026-11-10)
  • PR #2108 — docs clarifying document-skills snapshot/sync relationship (updated 2026-11-03)
  • PR #1975 / #1976 / #1977 — small, self-contained fixes from one contributor (pptx, webapp-testing, algorithmic-art), all referencing specific issues — likely fast-track candidates.

4. Skills Ecosystem Insight

The community's most concentrated demand is not new Skill ideas but reliability and trust in the existing Skill layer — fixing evaluation trigger rates, namespace impersonation, silent-success bugs, and context bloat in the core skills (skill-creator, docx, xlsx, claude-api, webapp-testing) that everyone depends on.

Data source: github.com/anthropics/skills, PRs and Issues as of 2026-11-12. Note: Comments: undefined for PRs indicates the field was not populated in the source dataset; ranking above weights update activity and issue cross-references.

Claude Code Community Digest — 2026-11-12

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases landed in the last 24 hours, but issue activity remains intense: a recurring entitlement sync bug is still locking individual Pro subscribers out of Claude Code, now spawning duplicate reports (#72027, #109155). On the feature side, the most-upvoted item today is the VS Code worktree session gap (#81024, 16 👍), while fresh reports highlight autocompact loop persistence on Windows (#108987) and cloud scheduled task prompt re-delivery (#109016). The single PR in the queue (#26230, path validation hooks) was closed without merge.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #72027 — Pro subscriber blocked by entitlement sync bug (CLOSED, 10 comments) — Individual Pro users hit "organization disabled" → "Max or Pro required." A long-running auth/entitlement desync that was finally closed today; worth watching for regression given #109155.
  2. #81024 — VS Code extension ignores git-worktree sessions (OPEN, 16 👍) — The extension hardcodes includeWorktrees: false, so worktree-based workflows lose session history. Highest community signal today.
  3. #98287 — Cowork scheduled tasks: permission classifier blocks owner-authorized sends (OPEN, 8 comments) — Cloud scheduled tasks refuse email sends that succeed interactively. Directly limits unattended automation.
  4. #98032 — macOS: turns hang ~6 min then ECONNRESET (OPEN) — Sudden-onset networking regression on one machine across all sessions; consistent failure shape makes it diagnosable.
  5. #84424 — Bash tool stdin-redirect regex is quote-unaware (OPEN, reproduced) — Quoted arguments containing < cause stdin to stay open and commands to hang via shell dotfiles. A subtle but high-impact tooling bug.
  6. #94446 — Desktop file viewer can't open links under additionalDirectories (OPEN, 6 👍) — Breaks multi-root workflows; links render but the viewer silently fails.
  7. #108955 — /model picker omits Fable 5.2 (OPEN, 5 👍) — Manual invocation works, picker doesn't. Small UI gap with outsized annoyance on Max plans.
  8. #108921 — Desktop auto mode refuses MCP calls after input rewrite (OPEN) — Auto-mode check runs before the app rewrites tool input, producing false "hook changed this call" refusals for archive_session/run_in_terminal.
  9. #108987 — Removing CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE doesn't stop autocompact loop (OPEN) — Env var persists in the process; requires restart. Painful for anyone testing compaction thresholds.
  10. #108745 — VS Code 2.1.322: telemetry off silently disables plugin sync (OPEN, regression) — Org-managed MCP servers/agents/skills vanish with no UI warning. A trust-eroding silent failure.

4. Key PR Progress

Only one PR was updated in the last 24 hours:

  1. #26230 — Feature/path validation hooks (CLOSED) — Proposed blocking relative paths from agent tool calls to strengthen sandboxing. Closed without merge; the underlying need for tighter sandbox path validation remains unaddressed.

No other PRs met the selection threshold, so no additional items are listed.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussions data was provided for this period.

6. Feature Request Trends

Distilled from today's issue set:

  • Session & workspace experience: git-worktree support in VS Code (#81024), native claude:// session links (#90290), statusLine row-sharing (#109141).
  • Cost & usage controls: advisor tool caching parameter exposure (#91110), toggle to disable cash Usage Credits on subscription plans (#92087), 1M context credit errors (#109160).
  • Voice & input UX: full voice mode with TTS, continuous listening, auto-submit (#102545); native spellcheck in VS Code chat input (#81814, 11 👍).
  • Web/Cloud parity: dismissing local command output in claude-code-web (#109151), read-only access to unattached public repos for composer install (#109162).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Entitlement/auth fragility: The Pro-subscriber lockout (#72027) closing the same day a duplicate appears (#109155) suggests the entitlement sync fix is not fully settled — a recurring trust issue for individual subscribers.
  • Silent failures in IDE integrations: Plugin sync dying when telemetry is off (#108745), gray session tabs after extension updates (#108714), and file viewer gaps (#94446) all share a theme: things break without telling the user.
  • Auto-mode/permission classifier false positives: Cowork email sends (#98287), desktop MCP refusals (#108921), and repeated "false positive" bug reports (#109163, #109164) point to permission systems that over-block legitimate, owner-authorized actions.
  • Bash tool edge cases: Quote-unaware stdin detection (#84424) continues to hang commands — a longstanding class of shell-integration bugs.
  • Config changes not taking effect live: Autocompact override persistence (#108987) adds to the pattern of settings.json changes requiring full restarts.

Note: The "Hot Issues" section includes the normally-capped 10 items from the 50 reported; issue #109155 was folded into the #72027 entry to avoid double-counting the same defect.

OpenAI Codex — openai/codex

OpenAI Codex Community Digest — 2026-11-12

1. Today's Highlights

The release pipeline remains fast-moving with seven version bumps in 24 hours (mostly alpha/point releases), headlined by rust-v0.167.2 shipping incremental tool updates by default on Google Cloud Vertex AI. Meanwhile, Windows desktop/sandbox reliability issues dominate the issue tracker — the top three issues by comment count are all Windows platform bugs, with #59895 (projects disappearing after app update) drawing 69 comments and 19 upvotes. The PR queue is almost entirely copyberry[bot]-generated fixes targeting sandbox permissions, MCP OAuth persistence, and model-state continuity, suggesting a coordinated hardening push.

2. Releases

Seven releases landed in the last 24h:

  • rust-v0.167.2 — the only one with substantive notes: Codex now sends tool updates incrementally by default on Google Cloud Vertex AI. Users can opt out via incremental_tools_legacy_gcp = false under [features] in config.toml (#60617, #60848).
  • Alpha/point releases with no release notes: rust-v0.170.0-alpha.2, rust-v0.170.0-alpha.1, rust-v0.169.0-alpha.11.1, rust-v0.169.0-alpha.11, rust-v0.169.0-alpha.10, rust-v0.167.0-alpha.4.3.

No changelog details were provided for the alpha channel, so breaking changes there are unverified.

3. Hot Issues (top 10 by engagement)

  1. #59895 — Windows: local projects disappear after app update + account switch (69 comments, 19 👍). The highest-engagement issue in the tracker. Users lose local project state after updating and switching back to a personal account. High emotional weight given data-loss implications.

  2. #45403 — Windows Full access: forced test-file cleanup denied with opaque "blocked by policy" (34 comments, 7 👍). A long-running (since September) discrepancy between the "Full access" UI promise and actual sandbox enforcement, with no review path for the user.

  3. #50520 — Windows sandbox: recurring helper_sandbox_lock_failed (21 comments). Permissions on .sandbox-bin regress to Modify, requiring manual ACL fixes. Classic recurrence bug.

  4. #59931 — Windows Desktop does not auto-connect enabled SSH host after restart (13 comments, 8 👍). Reproduced on two devices; erodes the "remote dev" workflow.

  5. #34946 — Allow Scheduled tasks to target SSH-connected hosts (10 comments, 11 👍). An enhancement with unusually strong support; users want automations over remote hosts.

  6. #59890 — Images 2.6 on Codex OAuth: no model selection, complexity/SVG ignored, GIF rejected (7 comments, 3 👍). New image models launched but are unusable for third-party OAuth clients — a feature-parity gap.

  7. #60594 — HTTP 400 for repeated image inputs with zstd compression on Windows (7 comments). Failing endpoint POST /backend-api/codex/responses, breaks chat continuation.

  8. #19669 — Slack connector keeps stale OAuth link after revoke/reconnect (7 comments). Auth-state hygiene issue affecting multi-Slack users; long-lived since April.

  9. #56951 — Codex ends turns after review/checkpoint milestones while acknowledging unfinished work (6 comments). Model-behavior bug: agent terminates turns mid-task — directly hurts autonomous execution trust.

  10. #58422 — Auto-review retains earlier authorization scope; exact-action approval unavailable (4 comments). Approval-scope over-retention is a security-adjacent concern.

4. Key PR Progress (top 10)

Note: all listed PRs are marked [CLOSED] and authored by copyberry[bot], indicating a batch of merged/superseded automated fixes.

  1. #60969 — Reconnect idle Cloud conversations after transient stream loss; holds queued input until the reply stream is usable.
  2. #60943 — Preserve file permissions during repeated Windows sandbox setup (directly addresses the class of bug in #50520).
  3. #60944 — Reconcile Windows runtime registration after service privilege errors.
  4. #60942 — Preserve thread-local model ID state across replay and compaction; recovers item ordinals from checkpoint replacement history.
  5. #60936 — Preserve legacy sandbox templates in TUI permission conversions (lossless PermissionProfile conversions).
  6. #60929 — Preserve Command Center task ownership across backend switches.
  7. #60905 — Keep same-named MCP servers separate across environments (disabled-by-default flag), fixing name-collision resolution.
  8. #60904 — Version answer display instructions into a v1 contract (show/hide/block) and restrict unsupported payloads.
  9. #60849 — Protect MCP OAuth persistence from stale credential writes (lock + revalidate) — relevant to auth staleness issues like #19669.
  10. #60848 — Enable incremental tool declarations by default for GCP (the change released in 0.167.2).

Honorable mentions: #60872 (Windows atomic writes via std::fs::rename), #60846 (thread search snippets for whitespace queries), #60871 (in-process init handshake race).

5. Hot Discussions

Ideas

  • #60954 — Let ChatGPT Pro users choose their usage window (5-hour vs. weekly). Mirrors a duplicate issue #60953; signals growing frustration with rate-limit ergonomics.

Q&A

  • #24717 — Recommended way to handle outdated/incorrect memories? No clear tooling to inspect, reset, or selectively delete stored memories.
  • #34373 — How to uninstall Codex CLI? (Answered.) Install script lacks an obvious counterpart for Arch Linux users.

Show and tell

  • #60116 — Pushary: answer Codex approvals from your phone / route a git push to a team lead. Uses native hooks + MCP; a hook-based policy gate before shell/apply_patch/MCP calls.
  • #60861 — claude-bulkhead: guard hooks for running Codex alongside other agents on one machine — born from agents killing each other's servers (e.g. pkill node).
  • #60834 — Concord: open-source MCP server for coordinating multiple Codex sessions on the same project (claim files, share context/handoffs).
  • #60852 — Desktop remoto RDP: control a Windows RDP session from Codex via screenshots + input injection.
  • #60818 — Running Codex + Claude Code from one Windows terminal (5–10 agents), with lessons learned.
  • #60762 — AGENTS.md Check: offline linter for AGENTS.md (merge markers, bidi controls, invalid UTF-8, repeated lines).
  • #60722 — TreeHarbor: preserve agent patches after workspace cleanup and open per-patch draft PRs.

Theme: The ecosystem is building multi-agent coordination and guardrail layers — shared MCP coordination, hook-based policy gates, cross-agent resource guards, and patch preservation.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Remote / SSH-based automation — Extending Scheduled tasks and auto-connect to SSH hosts (Issues #34946, #59931).
  • Adaptive subagent orchestration — Native orchestration tying subagents, model selection, reasoning effort and skills together with lower overhead (#51658).

Gemini CLI — google-gemini/gemini-cli

Gemini CLI Community Digest — 2026-11-12

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases landed in the past 24 hours, but community activity remains intense around the agent/subagent subsystem: recovery logic, browser agent reliability, and tool-scoping issues dominate the top issues. On the PR side, a wave of smaller but high-value fixes targets ACP mode (hooks, stderr flushing, hook-blocked prompts), Windows PowerShell event-loop blocking, and Unicode/ANSI handling in session previews. A recurring theme across both issues and PRs is enterprise telemetry hygiene and enterprise-safe metadata filtering.

2. Releases

None in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #20813 [CLOSED] – Account suspension in headless mode with custom system prompt (link) A p1 enterprise/security issue where a user was suspended for ToS violation while using headless mode. Closed, but with 14 comments and 3 👍 — signaling real concern about how the CLI's headless behavior interacts with Google's abuse systems.

  2. #22323 [OPEN] – Subagent MAX_TURNS misreported as GOAL success (link) codebase_investigator returns status: success / Termination Reason: GOAL even when it hit its turn cap. This is a correctness bug that silently hides agent interruption — dangerous for anyone relying on subagent outputs for automated workflows.

  3. #21409 [OPEN] – Generalist agent hangs indefinitely (link) Users report hangs up to an hour when the CLI defers to the generalist agent. Highest 👍 count (8) among the top issues, making it one of the most-felt pain points in the tracker.

  4. #19873 [OPEN] – Zero-dependency OS sandboxing + post-execution intent routing (link) A design proposal for letting Gemini 3 lean into its native bash affinity safely. Since Gemini 3 is trained as a bash-native model, this could become an architectural cornerstone for how the CLI executes tooling.

  5. #22745 [OPEN] – AST-aware file reads, search, and mapping (link) EPIC exploring AST-aware tooling to reduce tokens and misaligned reads. Closely tied to #22747's AST grep investigation — a clear signal that the team is moving toward semantic code navigation.

  6. #21968 [OPEN] – Gemini underuses skills and subagents (link) Anecdotal but credible: the model only uses custom skills/subagents when explicitly told. This undermines the entire extensibility story if users have to hand-hold the agent.

  7. #22267 [OPEN] – Browser Agent ignores settings.json overrides (link) maxTurns and other config are read by AgentRegistry but ignored at execution time. Config drift between registry and runner is a classic source of "why isn't my setting working?" bug reports.

  8. #21983 [OPEN] – Browser subagent fails on Wayland (link) Linux/Wayland users see the browser subagent terminate with a false "GOAL" success. Compounds SDK-level correctness concerns (see #22323) and limits the tool's viability on modern Linux desktops.

  9. #24246 [OPEN] – 400 error with >128 tools (link) The agent hits API limits when too many tools are in scope; the reporter's request that the agent "be a bit smarter about limiting tools" is a fair ask as MCP/extension ecosystems grow.

  10. #22672 [OPEN] – Agent should discourage destructive behavior (link) The model occasionally reaches for git reset or --force when safer options exist. Safety-adjacent, p2, and a likely candidate for policy/prompt-level guardrails.

Also worth watching: #20079 (symlinked agent files not recognized), #22186 (crash during get-shit-done output hook), #21763 (bug reports omit subagent context).

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #30010 [CLOSED] – Expose skill_name in safe tool metadata whitelist (link) Fixes a gap in enterprise telemetry: with logPrompts disabled, skill_name was previously filtered out, making skill usage invisible to org-level observability.

  2. #30009 [CLOSED] – OSS Exit Gate npm publishing workflow (link) Adds keyless WIF-based release pipeline for @google/gemini-cli, -a2a-server, and -core. Long-term reliability win for release engineering.

  3. #30003 / #30250 [CLOSED] – ${VAR:-default} semantics fixed (link) Aligns env var expansion with Bash when a variable is set but empty. Small but frequently-hit footgun for settings.json users.

  4. #30148 [OPEN] – Fire SessionStart and Notification hooks in ACP mode (link) Brings ACP sessions up to parity with interactive mode for hook lifecycle events.

  5. #30134 [OPEN] – Report hook-blocked prompts over ACP (link) ACP clients previously saw an empty end_turn when a hook denied a prompt. Now surfaces the block reason as an agent_message_chunk.

  6. #30144 [OPEN] – Initialize output listeners and flush stderr in ACP mode (link) Fixes silent stderr in ACP sessions — hook logs and warnings now appear in real time instead of at process exit.

  7. #30247 [OPEN] – Avoid blocking PowerShell parsing during shell checks (link) Windows UX fix: synchronous PS startup/AST parsing froze the Thinking spinner. Async parsing restores responsiveness.

  8. #30228 [CLOSED] – Preserve interrupted placeholder after empty model responses (link) Fixes 400 Bad Request ("Requests ending with a model turn are not supported") and prompt fusion bugs after empty/thought-only model turns.

  9. #30176 [CLOSED] – Preserve selected worktree across auth restarts (link) --worktree selections now survive RELAUNCH_EXIT_CODE = 199. Regression-class fix that resolves a documented issue (#30078).

  10. #29546 [OPEN] – Support /skill-name activation in non-interactive mode (link) Registers SkillCommandLoader in the non-interactive path, extending skill usage to scripts and CI — tagged help wanted.

Also notable: #30220 (Unicode/ANSI preservation in session previews), #30246 (quote IDE CLI path for cmd.exe on Windows).

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided in the source pull. This section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

Distilling across the top 30 issues:

  • AST-aware code navigation — #22745, #22746, #22747. Multiple issues investigate AST greps and semantic search to cut tokens and misaligned reads. This is the most coherent multi-issue research direction in the tracker.
  • Smarter tool scoping — #24246 (>128 tools → 400 error) and #19873 (post-execution intent routing) both point to a need for dynamic tool selection.
  • Persistent, file-based task tracking — #18836 (deprecate WriteToDo for CRUD-based persistent tasks) and #21000 (native file tools for the task tracker).
  • Subagent observability & debuggability — #22598 (/chat share subagent trajectory), #21763 (subagent context in bug reports), #20266-adjacent workstreams.
  • Parallel/shared-memory subagents — #18287 (currently blocked pending parallel subagent logic).
  • Per-workspace policy overrides — #18397 asks for workspace-scoped policies beyond global scope.
  • Agent self-awareness — #21432 asks the CLI to accurately know its own flags, hotkeys, and self-invocation patterns.
  • Browser agent resilience — #22232 (session takeover/lock recovery), #22267 (settings overrides honored), #21983 (Wayland).

7. Developer Pain Points

Recurring frustrations across the issue corpus:

  1. Silent subagent failures — Issues #22323 and #21983 both show agents reporting "GOAL/success" when they actually failed or hit a turn cap. This undermines trust in multi-agent pipelines and is the most damaging category of bug for power users.
  2. Hangs and deadlocks — #21409 (generalist agent hangs up to an hour) and #22465 (vite interactive prompt hang) point to gaps in interactive-prompt handling and turn management.
  3. Config not honored at runtime — #22267 (browser agent ignores settings.json) and #20079 (symlinks not recognized) suggest an inconsistency between discovery/registration and execution layers.
  4. Enterprise/ToS anxiety — #20813 (headless mode suspension) and the PR #30010 telemetry work reveal tension between enterprise telemetry needs and abuse-system false positives.
  5. Platform-specific breakage — Wayland (#21983), Windows PowerShell freezes (#30247), cmd.exe path quoting (#30246), non-UTF-8 web fetch (#27980). Cross-platform polish remains a backlog.
  6. Token/context bloat — #19561 ("tactful extraction" for surgical reads), #22745, and the AST EPICs all stem from frustration with ~36.6k context baselines and +15k/turn file-read spikes.
  7. Agent misunderstanding its own capabilities — #21968 (doesn't invoke skills/spawn subagents) and #21432 (should be its own expert guide) reflect a gap between the platform's extensibility surface and model behavior.

1. Today's Highlights

Qwen Code 1.0 Preview (v1.0.0-preview) has landed, merging Qoder and Qwen Code agent capabilities for end-to-end code understanding, implementation, debugging, and testing. Meanwhile, the community is actively stress-testing the event-bus agent loop refactor and Managed Agent parity features (web terminal, client filesystems, durable /loop wakeups). CI stability remains the dominant operational concern, with several flaky-test and lint-gate issues surfacing in the last 24 hours.

2. Releases

v1.0.0-preview — Release page

  • Merges agent capabilities from Qoder and Qwen Code for code understanding, implementation, debugging, and testing.
  • Supports Qwen and Qoder accounts.
  • ⚠️ Interfaces, configuration options, and behaviors may change during the Preview period.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate — no test identified (325 comments). The highest-traffic issue in the tracker; a long-running CI gate failure with no attributable test. Its comment volume signals sustained bot/CI churn rather than human discussion.

  2. #11680 — E2E Tests — no test identified (48 comments). Persistent main-branch E2E failures tracked per commit; symptomatic of broader CI signal-to-noise problems.

  3. #11678 — Qwen Code CI — Windows Node 22.x failure (26 comments, autofix/in-progress). Windows-specific test failures remain a recurring platform gap.

  4. #13009 — cron-tools registration failure (21 comments, status/ready-for-agent, autofix/approved). A concrete, scoped bug now queued for automated fix — representative of the project's autofix pipeline maturing.

  5. #16425 (CLOSED) — Workflow agent permission approval never renders; run hangs indefinitely (10 comments, P1). A serious UX/correctness bug in multi-agent workflows where permission prompts fire but never render, leaving status bars stuck. Now closed — worth noting as the resolution lands.

  6. #16915 — Task reports two errors and cannot continue (7 comments). User-facing connection interruption to the model service; a recurring 1.x stability complaint.

  7. #124 — Self-hosted Qwen3-Coder tool calls fail almost always (7 comments, 7 👍). The most-upvoted issue shown; self-hosting tool-call reliability remains an open sore for the OSS deployment community.

  8. #15861 — Web-shell host-directory-picker smoke times out, PR-independent (7 comments, P1). A deterministic E2E failure causing every PR to pay a re-attribution cost — directly impacting contributor throughput.

  9. #16982 — /rewind after /cd restores checkpoint into wrong working directory (P1, ready-for-human). A data-loss-class bug: silently overwrites unrelated files. High severity for session management.

  10. #16767 — Spurious "previous request was interrupted" banner on tool-call turn settle (P2). Web Shell falsely signals interruption when a turn ends cleanly on a tool call — a noisy UX regression in daemon sessions.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #16938 — Re-express the agent loop on the event bus (opt-in). Refactors the shared agent loop into Conversation/Llm/Tool handlers plus a host adapter on event-bus primitives — architectural groundwork for the 1.0 agent model.

  2. #16866 — Managed Web Terminal. Adds an interactive web terminal relayed byte-for-byte via WebSocket to the Runtime worker PTY, closing the web_terminal Managed parity gap.

  3. #16844 — Register client filesystems into managed sessions. Lets Managed Agent sessions access the browser user's local filesystem via a Java-mediated MCP bridge (workaround for no WebSocket tunnels in the hosted harness).

  4. #16835 — Durable self-paced /loop wakeups for Managed Sessions. Moves wakeups from in-memory timers to durable Session-journal inputs with earliest-start admission.

  5. #16653 — Enforce Read deny rules on grep and glob results. Closes a permission leak where ripgrep/grep/glob could return denied content before truncation/formatting.

  6. #16895 — Bound post-compaction restoration by the context window. Fixes the file-content restoration budget to account for route-scoped server ceilings and CJK token density.

  7. #16926 — Publish file-history backups atomically. Ports crash-safe backup capture from the preview branch — pilot of the "split preview features into main PRs" track.

  8. #16877 — Manual session PR binding (/pr command + Web Shell dialog). Adds explicit user-driven PR binding for TUI, headless CLI, and daemon sessions.

  9. #16865 — Gate reconcile record read and batch segment plan (perf). Skips redundant delivery-record reads when the ledger already has receipts — a managed-agent reconcile optimization.

  10. #16804 — Configure DingTalk webhooks and scheduled delivery targets. Extends Web Shell Channels with DingTalk app-bot and webhook methods plus delivery targets.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussion data was provided in the source dataset, so this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

Distilled from Issues and PRs, the most-requested directions are:

  • Verification as a core mechanism — #16941 proposes a verify-then-repair loop with a clean-context verifier subagent.
  • Programmatic tool calling — #16944 asks the agent to orchestrate tools as code inside the sandbox and return only results.
  • Web Shell polish & extensibility — host content slots in the model picker (#16893), contact-based channel allowlists (#16931), focus management (#16980), and session search improvements (#16779).
  • Managed Agent parity — web terminal, client filesystems, durable loop wakeups, and shared external workspaces (#16023).
  • Multi-agent workflows — the roadmap label on #16425 signals demand for reliable workflow-agent permission handling.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • CI signal-to-noise: The top issues by comment count are all CI failure reports (#14724, #11680, #11678). Flaky tests and unattributable failures dominate bot activity, and PR-independent failures like #15861 tax every contributor.
  • Model connection instability: Repeated reports of interrupted model service connections during execution (#16915, #16908), often without detailed logs.
  • Self-hosting friction: Tool calls failing with self-hosted Qwen3-Coder (#124) remains the top-voted issue shown, limiting OSS deployment adoption.
  • Permission & data-safety correctness: Read deny rules leaking through search results (#16653) and /rewind restoring into the wrong directory (#16982) are trust-eroding bugs.
  • Docs drift: Stale guidance such as "restart after adding an MCP server" (#16925) when hot-reload already works.
  • Platform quirks: macOS symlink/argv handling causing silent lint no-ops (#16954) and glob being unable to match directories (#16921).

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-12

Issues: 476 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-12 02:12 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-12

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains in a very high-velocity maintenance phase: 476 issues and 500 PRs updated in the last 24 hours, with a roughly even open/closed split (265/211 issues; 313/187 PRs). A new beta (v2026.11.5-beta.2) shipped, headlined by paged bidirectional conversation history and bounded archive reads. The day's PR traffic is dominated by a maintainer-led stability push (principally steipete) to remove synchronous filesystem/DB work from the Gateway event loop — a coherent response to the project's most persistent class of complaints (startup stalls, event-loop blocking, memory bloat). However, the issue tracker continues to carry a heavy load of P0/P1 crash-loop, message-loss, and session-state defects, several of them long-lived (60–150+ days), indicating that fix throughput is not yet keeping pace with reported reliability debt. Overall: healthy contribution volume, elevated unresolved reliability risk.

2. Releases

v2026.11.5-beta.2 (1 new release)

Highlights

  • Paged conversation history (both directions) — large conversations remain browsable with visible history boundaries and bounded archive reads, preventing unbounded memory/IO when opening long sessions. (#188450, #188483, #188557, #188372, #190690) — authored by @steipete, thanks @xydt-tanshanshan.
  • macOS app preserves saved secrets across restarts.

Breaking Changes / Migration Notes

  • No explicit breaking changes or migration steps are documented in the release notes.
  • Caveat (from the issue tracker): the 2026.9.6 plugin source-capture change is still the root cause of several open P0/P1 regressions (Gateway blocking, Windows staging explosion). Users upgrading from ≤2026.9.5 on Windows or with large external plugins should treat 2026.11.x as not yet verified clean for those configurations (see §5).

3. Project Progress

187 PRs merged/closed and 211 issues closed in the 24h window. Notable closed items today:

  • [CLOSED] #166634 — Late reclamation commit checkpoint failure leaving agents unavailable after crash recovery (clawsweeper:not-repro-on-main). Link
  • [CLOSED] #159638 — Excessive SQLite store/read worker churn (~7 workers/min, 512 MB each) pinning V8 CPU. Link
  • [CLOSED] #173095 — Control UI session sidebar empty on cold start (sessions.list never requested). Link
  • [CLOSED] #179481 — doctor --fix blocked by active agent-DB lease during transcript-directives migration. Link
  • [CLOSED] #179676 — Control UI pasted text (>1,000 chars) lost on subsequent turns. Link
  • [CLOSED] #181958 — package-doctor update failure (2026.10.3). Link

Active fix PRs advancing (open):

  • #197445, #197446, #197455, #197461 (steipete) — a coordinated set removing blocking directory-watch, DB-restat, lock-polling, and patch-file-check operations from the Gateway thread. PR #197445 · PR #197446 · PR #197455 · PR #197461
  • #197457 — Shorten Gateway restart when active commands need cleanup. Link
  • #197427 — Preserve final-delivery recovery custody after RPC writer claim. Link
  • #197448 — Batch content searches across shared Git history (fixes lazy-fetch/promisor-pack explosion). Link
  • #195092 — Unicode NFC/NFD canonical matching in knowledge search. Link
  • #194688 — Feishu isolated topics process messages concurrently. Link

Feature work in flight: macOS one-ID approval setup (#197421), explicit bounded Deep Research workflow (#197453), continuation/context-pressure tools (#129388), GitHub integration → plugin migration (#192350).

4. Community Hot Topics

Most-commented issues in the window (links included):

  1. #160959 — [OPEN, P0, crash-loop] Gateway blocks for minutes capturing large external plugins (81 comments). The single hottest thread. Root cause: plugin source-capture landed in 2026.9.6. Deep plugin/dependency trees stall the event loop at startup and on runtime republish. Link
  2. #164294 — [OPEN, P2] Gateway state DB WAL auto-checkpoint never completes (40 comments). Checkpoint permanently blocked by a reader; frames accumulate (866/17,091 onward). Link
  3. #170956 — [OPEN, P0] Windows slow startup, unclean plugin shutdown, schtasks permission errors (31 comments). Restarts/updates fail repeatedly; occasional disconnect (1006). Link
  4. #168955 — [OPEN, P1] Startup regression 2026.10.1: ~1030s vs ~410s ready (Windows) — sidecars.control-ui-assets blocks 477s (21 comments). Link
  5. #125764 — [OPEN, P1, message-loss] Telegram adapter dead-letters failed outbound sends after one attempt (14 comments, 1 👍). Silent loss of announce/completion replies, no retry, no reconcileUnknownSend. Link
  6. #145309 — [CLOSED] claude-cli ignores CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (14 comments, 2 👍). Missing-transcript resets and session failover. Link
  7. #144809 — [OPEN, P1] claude-cli turns longer than RUN_STALE_TAKEOVER_MS lose entire reply (14 comments). Link

Underlying needs analysis: Community attention clusters around three themes — (a) Gateway event-loop responsiveness (plugin capture, WAL checkpoint, directory watching, DB restat), (b) Windows as a second-class platform (schtasks, staging explosion, 2.5× startup regression), and (c) silent message loss on channel adapters (Telegram, claude-cli). The high comment counts on months-old P0 threads signal that users are still waiting, not just discussing.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (fix PR noted where one exists):

Severity Issue Summary Fix PR?
P0 #160959 Gateway blocks minutes capturing large external plugins (2026.9.6 regression) — 81 comments None new
P0 #170956 Windows schtasks/startup/shutdown unreliability; restarts fail often None new
P0 #178441 Owner Telegram held by providerReview, no recovery action None
P0 #194664 Codex "protected continuation" blocks all follow-ups while Stop reports no active run (2026.11.1) None
P0 #146791 iOS App Store build never publishes push.apns.register — push broken None
P1 #168955 Windows startup regression ~410s → ~1030s None
P1 #125764 Telegram outbound send dead-lettered after 1 attempt (silent loss) None
P1 #144809 claude-cli long turns lose full reply None
P1 #181432 Baseline RSS ~300 MB → 1.89 GB (2026.10.5); SQLite tx timeouts None
P1 #168101 Retry-After ignores maxRetryDelayMs after tool call; lane held None
P1 #191818 claude-cli "no recorded inference account" in scheduled automation; backport #180492 requested Partially (backport)
P1 #181662 npm update keeps Gateway stopped ~19 min, growing each release None
P1 #145690 Subagent completion releases runtime generation; next lane task fails ~15ms, user message dropped None
P2 #164294 State DB WAL checkpoint never completes None
P2 #162585 Windows plugin staging re-materializes self, 290 MB → 612 MB+/24 min None

Observations: A large share of these are regressions introduced by 2026.9.6/2026.10.x and are marked clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr — i.e., no fix PR is queued. However, the maintainer's blocking-I/O PR cluster this week (#197445/#197446/#197455/#197457/#197461, plus #159638's close) directly targets the class of defect behind #160959 and #164294, so incremental relief is plausibly landing in 2026.11.5.x.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Active user-requested features, ordered by likelihood of near-term adoption:

  • #192009 — Explicitly authorize cross-provider cron fallback accounts (P2, 11 comments, diamond-lobster rating). High-signal request; low architectural risk — a plausible candidate for a near-future beta since model fallback plumbing already exists. Link
  • #179954 — Configurable per-entry chunking for memory/ files (P3, diamond-lobster). memory-core already has per-entry chunking, so this is a narrow extension — cheap to ship. Link
  • #176273 — Native progress-card SDK + trusted-plugin admission (P2, security-labeled). Blocked on product/security decision. Link
  • #143387 — Android notification QoL (session-aware, labels, cross-device suppression). Link
  • #170562 — Doctor recovery for stranded requester-settle wake. Operator recovery affordance; follows from #154252. Link
  • #169428 — Expose auth profile (model.auth_label) in usage footer (P3, fix-shape-clear). Nearly a one-line template change. Link
  • #164355 — Plugin hook to append content after tool results in-flight. Architectural; likely to linger. Link

Prediction: The next 1–2 betas are more likely to consolidate the I/O-blocking fixes and ship small, clear-shape features (#169428, #179954, possibly #192009) than to land large architectural requests (#176273, #164355).

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (dominant):

  • Startup/restart reliability on Windows — multiple independent reporters (#170956, #168955, #162585) describe minutes-scale startup, failed restarts, and staged plugin trees growing unbounded. Satisfaction here is visibly low ("only after many retries").
  • Silent message loss — Telegram (#125764), claude-cli (#144809, #191818), and dashboard sessions (#144876) can drop replies with no user-visible error. This is the most trust-eroding class.
  • Resource bloat — RSS jumping to ~1.9 GB (#181432) and worker/memory churn (#159638, #181432) hit self-hosters on ARM64/small hosts hardest.
  • UI fidelity — path truncation and visible internal context injections (#172986, #165041) are minor but frequently cited friction.
  • Update downtime — npm updates keeping the Gateway down ~19 min (#181662) undermines the "always-on assistant" premise.

Positive signals:

  • Strong engagement: 81/40/31-comment threads show a vocal, invested user base.
  • The paged conversation history feature in 2026.11.5-beta.2 responds directly to long-session browsability complaints — a well-received direction.
  • Users actively file high-quality repros (source-repro tags, logs, version pins), reducing maintainer triage cost.

Net sentiment: Frustration concentrated on reliability of the gateway lifecycle and message delivery, not on the core agent capabilities — users clearly like the product enough to keep debugging it.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-lived, high-importance items needing maintainer attention (age as of 2026-11-12):

  • #91931 (created 2026-06-10, ~155 days open, P1, diamond lobster) — Preseeded SOUL/IDENTITY/USER files auto-complete bootstrap and delete user-provided BOOTSTRAP.md before first run. Data-loss + onboarding bug with a clear fix-shape flag but no fix PR. Link
  • #101929 (2026-07-08, ~127 days) — context-overflow estimator over-counts 2.3–2.6× vs billed usage; partial main-branch repair (#168338) but issue still open. Link
  • #125764 (2026-08-18, ~86 days, P1) — Telegram dead-lettering after single attempt. High blast radius, no fix PR. Link
  • #132767 (2026-08-29, ~75 days) — Generic CLI host assembles systemPromptAddition one turn late; prior source fix (#100984) closed without merge, no issue filed — process gap worth revisiting. Link
  • #141172 (2026-09-07, ~66 days) — Runs dying pre-first-commit leak agent.run.started forever; FK failures, no agent.run.finished. Link
  • #129388 (PR, opened 2026-08-25, ~79 days, XL) — Context-pressure-aware continuation tools; large, security-sensitive, stuck in needs proof. Link
  • #155860 (PR, opened 2026-09-22, ~51 days) — Let memory slot owner report its own dreaming status; waits on author. Link

Recommendation: #91931 and #125764 are the two backlog items with the highest ratio of user impact to remaining work; both have fix-shape-clear/source-repro signal and neither has an open fix PR.

Data source: github.com/openclaw/openclaw — window 2026-11-11 → 2026-11-12. Comment/reaction counts reflect snapshot at generation time; undefined comment counts on PRs indicate the field was not returned in the source data.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Assistant / Agent OSS Ecosystem

Snapshot date: 2026-11-12 | Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent open-source landscape on 2026-11-12 is post-hype and consolidation-heavy: reference implementations have shipped multi-user, multi-channel, plugin-extensible runtimes, and the community's energy has shifted from "what can an agent do" to "can I trust it in production." Five projects span a wide maturity gradient — from OpenClaw's ~476 issue / 500 PR daily cadence to IronClaw's zero activity — but they share a common failure narrative: gateway lifecycle reliability, message-delivery integrity, and observability of agent failure. A second thematic wave is visible across QwenPaw, Hermes, and ZeroClaw: plugin/channel abstraction is the dominant refactor, and it is temporarily regressing previously-working integrations. Security posture (HMAC, consent gates, tripwire plugins, dependency advisories) is now a first-class community contribution category rather than a niche. Net signal: the ecosystem's bottleneck has moved from capability to operational trust.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues (24h) PRs (24h) Release Status Health Score*
OpenClaw 476 updated (265 open / 211 closed) 500 updated (313 open / 187 closed) v2026.11.5-beta.2 — active pre-stable line B+ — high velocity, elevated unresolved P0 debt
Hermes Agent 50 updated (0 closed) 50 updated (0 merged / 0 closed) No release; testing against v0.23.0 C+ — active PR queue, but zero merge throughput + regression debt
IronClaw 0 0 None N/A — dormant
QwenPaw 7 updated 32 updated (5 closed incl. 8-month PR) v2.3.0 Stable shipped; beta.4 verification closed clean B — strong release cadence, plugin-migration regressions open
ZeroClaw 8 updated (0 closed, all open) 49 updated (45 open, 4 merged/closed) v0.9.0 — multi-user OIDC release B- — solid direction, review-capacity bottleneck (45:4)

* Health score synthesizes velocity, merge/close throughput, release hygiene, unfixed critical bugs, and backlog age from the underlying digests.

Reading the table:

  • OpenClaw is an order of magnitude larger in raw activity than any peer, and is the only project shipping a beta and closing ~200 issues/day.
  • Hermes and ZeroClaw both show a review throughput deficit (0 and 4 merges respectively) despite large open queues — the ecosystem's most replicable anti-pattern.
  • QwenPaw is the only project that shipped a stable release on the window, but it is also the only one with an explicit release-blocking regression cluster (channel plugins).
  • IronClaw is effectively inactive and should be treated as a watch-list outlier, not a comparator.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs peers:

  • Scale of contribution surface. OpenClaw's 24h window (~976 issue+PR updates) exceeds the combined totals of Hermes, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw by roughly 8×. This produces faster triage feedback loops, richer reproduction data, and a wider plugin ecosystem — its biggest structural moat.
  • Coherent maintainer-led technical direction. The steipete-authored blocking-I/O PR cluster (#197445/#197446/#197455/#197457/#197461) is a rare example of class-level remediation targeting the root cause (synchronous FS/DB on the Gateway event loop) rather than per-symptom patching. No peer shows a comparable coordinated hardening thrust except Hermes' c2h5oh sec-marathon, which is narrower in scope.
  • Mature release cadence. Weekly beta cadence with documented caveats (e.g., the 2026.9.6 plugin source-capture regression) beats "no release + 50 open PRs" by every operational metric.

Technical approach differences:

  • OpenClaw's architecture is gateway-centric with bidirectional conversation history and bounded archive reads — i.e., it optimizes for long-session fidelity, which peers do not yet engineer for explicitly. Hermes' unified gateway (#106742) is thematically similar but landed before the reliability hardening, which is precisely why Hermes is currently drowning in cross-surface regressions.
  • OpenClaw leans on a SQLite state DB with WAL — a source of both its resilience and its worst latency complaints (#164294, #181432). ZeroClaw uses runtime-trace.jsonl + daemon with similar observability gaps (#12391). Neither has solved "durable, cheap, queryable runtime state."

Community size comparison:

  • Hot-thread intensity: OpenClaw's top thread has 81 comments; Hermes' top thread has 60; ZeroClaw's top thread has 6. By engaged-user proxy, OpenClaw is the largest and most argumentative community by roughly an order of magnitude.
  • Backlog age distribution: OpenClaw's oldest P1s run 150+ days (#91931); Hermes' top PR is ~5 months (#40850); ZeroClaw's CI issue is ~5 months (#7461). OpenClaw's absolute backlog is larger, but its relative closure rate (~44% of updated issues closed in 24h) is the highest in the cohort.

Verdict: OpenClaw is the de-facto reference implementation — the project whose failure modes peers will inherit and whose fixes they will copy. Its risk is breadth-induced triage dilution, not direction.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Five requirements recur across ≥2 projects and constitute the ecosystem's emerging common agenda:

(a) Gateway / daemon event-loop responsiveness under load.

  • OpenClaw: plugin source-capture blocking minutes at startup (#160959), WAL checkpoint never completing (#164294), DB-restat/directory-watch blocking (#197445–#197461).
  • Hermes: unified-gateway regression set (#143547), Windows event-loop stalls under concurrent Kanban workers (#152364), multiplexed dashboard losing MCP tools after failed teardown (#152175).
  • ZeroClaw: runtime-trace.jsonl dropping events across daemon restarts (#12391), cron receipt recovery clearing a newer live firer's claim (#152296).
  • Shared need: cooperative async I/O with bounded, observable backpressure — and a standard way to attribute stalls to a specific subsystem.

(b) Silent message / delivery loss.

  • OpenClaw: Telegram outbound dead-lettered after one attempt (#125764), claude-cli long turns dropping replies (#144809), iOS APNs never registering (#146791).
  • Hermes: Weixin voice message stuck in session_admissions (#152365), 0-byte state.db breaking bot delivery (#153048), Discord handoff thread type defaulting wrong (#95670).
  • Shared need: delivery reconciliation with retry budgets and user-visible failure surfaces — currently absent everywhere.

(c) Plugin / channel abstraction hardening.

  • QwenPaw: channel plugin extraction producing CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED (#8669), missing HOME/QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR on Linux (#8682), Matrix multi-workspace race (#8538).
  • Hermes: plugin generation lock-pin migration (#154165), plugin catalog churn (Cutroom, EarnFi, snare).
  • OpenClaw: GitHub integration → plugin migration (#192350), trusted-plugin admission (#176273).
  • ZeroClaw: SOP/delegate tool-ceiling and shared-tmp hardening (#12394, #154127-equivalent PRs).
  • Shared need: a formal plugin host↔worker contract — env propagation, health-check timing, state initialization, and capability scoping — before migration can be called stable.

(d) Cost, billing, and usage observability.

  • Hermes: fallback model persisted to session state survives reload (#152333 — silent billing continuation), per-session cost display demanded (#93951).
  • OpenClaw: RSS bloat 300 MB → 1.89 GB (#181432), worker churn (#159638), update downtime ~19 min (#181662).
  • ZeroClaw: operator override for exceeded cost limit only via restart (#11589).
  • Shared need: real-time, per-session cost and resource telemetry with user-controllable bounds.

(e) Cron / automation semantics correctness.

  • ZeroClaw: cron reports Ok while agent concludes BLOCKED (#12397).
  • OpenClaw: cross-provider cron fallback authorization requested (#192009), stale-takeover losses (#144809), subagent completion races (#145690).
  • Hermes: cron receipt recovery corrupting live firer (#152296), Kanban blocker_auth permanent stall (#119070).
  • Shared need: distinct execution-status and task-outcome channels — the current conflation is a root cause across three projects.

5. Differentiation Analysis

Dimension OpenClaw Hermes Agent QwenPaw ZeroClaw
Primary focus General-purpose reference runtime; long-session fidelity Unified multi-surface gateway (CLI/TUI/Desktop/bots/cron) Consumer + enterprise messaging channels; local decision models Self-hosted / home-lab daemon; multi-tenant auth
Target user Broad OSS dev/self-hoster base Multi-surface power users + Desktop users Enterprise messaging (Feishu/WeChat/Matrix/DingTalk/QQ) + desktop Home-lab operators, multi-user self-hosts
Architecture Gateway + SQLite/WAL state DB; plugin source-capture Single unified gateway process (~all surfaces) Plugin-extracted subsystems (channels, MCP, models, agents) Rust daemon + runtime-trace.jsonl + cron dispatcher
Release posture Weekly betas with explicit caveats No release this window; ~50 unmerged PRs Stable v2.3.0 shipped; patch expected v0.9.0 shipped; 45-PR review queue
Standout differentiator Paged bidirectional history + bounded archive reads; maintainer-led blocking-I/O remediation Desktop redesign; durable subagent continuation; sec-marathon Piccolo 4B/9B/27B local decision models; OpenSandbox cloud backend First multi-user OIDC sign-in; scoped per-account chat
Biggest own-goal 2026.9.6 plugin regression still latent on Windows Merged unified gateway without routing isolation Plugin migration regressed channels that previously worked Review backlog aging XL PRs past 2 months

Key architectural divergence: OpenClaw and Hermes both bet on a single gateway process but arrive there from opposite directions — OpenClaw layered reliability fixes on top of a mature gateway; Hermes merged surfaces into a gateway and is now paying the integration tax. QwenPaw is decomposing out of a monolith into plugins — the opposite trajectory. ZeroClaw alone has kept a tight core + thin channel surface, which likely explains its cleaner security posture and its smaller raw bug count, at the cost of ecosystem breadth.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Tier 1 — Rapid iteration at scale (OpenClaw). ~200 issue closes/day, weekly betas, coordinated maintainer hardening PRs. Mature triage pipeline; primary risk is reliability debt not yet converted to fixes (multiple P0s with clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr).

Tier 2 — High activity, throughput-limited (Hermes, ZeroClaw).

  • Hermes has the broadest surface area and the deepest security workstream (sec-marathon: consent gates, HMAC hardening, per-session bearer auth, tmp hardening) but zero merges in 24h against 50 open PRs — a textbook review-capacity bottleneck.
  • ZeroClaw shipped a substantive v0.9.0 (117 commits, 22 contributors) with same-day security patching (#12392), and its community files precise, evidence-backed production reports — but sits at a 45:4 open:closed PR ratio and four unfixed S1/S2 bugs. Direction is right; throughput is the constraint.

Tier 3 — Stabilizing, release-verified (QwenPaw). Shipped stable v2.3.0, closed an 8-month contributor PR (#1972), and closed a beta.4 verification cleanly. But the same window shows an open stable release-verification issue (#8681) and a release-blocking channel regression cluster — so it is simultaneously the most release-mature and the most exposed project in the cohort.

Tier 4 — Dormant (IronClaw). Zero activity; watch-list only.

Momentum synthesis: The ecosystem has two active engineering cultures — OpenClaw's "close more than you open" pipeline and a wider "open more than you close" pattern at Hermes/ZeroClaw. QwenPaw is the only mid-tier project executing a verification-gated release process, which is the model the other three will likely need to adopt as they approach stable.

7. Trend Signals

For AI agent developers and decision-makers, the 2026-11-12 window surfaces six durable signals:

  1. Reliability is the product, not the feature. Every project's top pain points are lifecycle/delivery/observability failures — not missing capabilities. Budget for gateway hardening, delivery reconciliation, and structured trace integrity before new integrations.

  2. The "agent hides why it failed" anti-pattern is ecosystem-wide. ZeroClaw's swallowed stderr (#12390), Hermes' stuck session_admissions (#152365), OpenClaw's Telegram dead-lettering (#125764), and ZeroClaw's cron Ok-despite-BLOCKED (#12397) are the same failure mode wearing four costumes. A shared open standard for agent failure surfaces (structured outcome + reason + recovery hint) is overdue.

  3. Plugin/channel extraction is high-risk, high-return — treat it as a stability project. QwenPaw's channel regressions (#8669, #8538, #8682), Hermes' plugin lock-pin migration (#154165), and OpenClaw's GitHub-to-plugin move (#192350) all show the same pattern: the migration itself causes more incidents than the pluginized subsystem did pre-migration. Harden the host↔worker contract (env vars, health checks, startup timing) before the refactor.

  4. Security is now a community contribution category, not a vendor feature. Same-day RUSTSEC patches (ZeroClaw #12392), coordinated sec-marathon PRs (Hermes #153698–#154137), and community prompt-injection tripwires (snare #153380) indicate a maturing supply chain. Expect security-labeled PRs to be a leading indicator of project health.

  5. Cost/billing observability is the next trust frontier. Hermes users see fallback providers silently billing (#152333); OpenClaw users see RSS quadruple (#181432); ZeroClaw users can only escape cost limits via restart (#11589). Per-session, real-time cost and resource display — with hard bounds — will differentiate projects with paid-API users.

  6. Review throughput, not contributor interest, is the ecosystem bottleneck. Hermes (0 merges / 50 open PRs), ZeroClaw (4 / 45), and QwenPaw's long-review queue (#8236, #8409, #8601) show healthy contribution supply meeting limited review capacity. Projects that invest in reviewer tooling, batched-review workflows, or paid maintainer bandwidth will compound; those that don't will accumulate bit-rotting XL PRs and contributor churn.

Bottom line for builders: OpenClaw is the ecosystem's reference and its most active hardening ground; Hermes is the most architecturally ambitious and most regression-exposed; QwenPaw is the enterprise-channel and local-model specialist executing the cleanest release discipline; ZeroClaw is the rust-native self-hosting platform with the best security reflexes and the worst review backlog. The shared agenda — event-loop responsiveness, delivery reconciliation, plugin contract hardening, cost observability, and cron semantics — is the de-facto 2027 roadmap for the category, whether or not the projects coordinate on it.

  • #12394 — Bound SOP step agent's tool ceiling to its actual registry + pin deferred-MCP seal input (follow-up hardening, likely near-term).
  • #9814 — Native XMPP/Prosody channel (PR #11847 already open — highest-probability landing feature).
  • #7461 — Windows/macOS test CI (accepted, in-progress, but stalled since June).

Roadmap prediction for next release (v0.9.x / v0.10):

  1. XMPP channel via PR #11847 — issue + implementation both active.
  2. Cron outcome semantics (#12397) — cheap, user-visible correctness win.
  3. Shell/SSH hardening — PR #11869 (transport reuse) + #11994 (bash grammar security) form a coherent cluster.
  4. Multi-model provider profiles (PR #9809, open since August, XL) — a long-running architectural item that would reshape provider config.
  5. SOP/delegate sealing (#12394, PR #10391) — security-boundary work with Core Team attention.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (dissatisfaction):

  • "The agent only learns that 'something failed' and cannot tell why." — #12390 (swallowed stderr). A direct hit on agent debuggability.
  • "The whole step never happened." — #8794, on interruption erasing context. Trust-eroding for interactive sessions.
  • "Multi-hour coverage gaps… even though agent work provably continued." — #12391, trace integrity on production daemons.
  • "Ok in the dashboard even when the agent explicitly concludes BLOCKED." — #12397, misleading automation status.

Use cases visible in the data:

  • Home-lab / low-resource self-hosting (XMPP/Prosody request, Windows service deployment).
  • Chrome DevTools MCP automation via cron (reproduction in #12397).
  • Multi-worktree ZeroCode workflows hitting the 8-session cap (PR #11731).
  • Multi-user self-hosted deployments (the entire v0.9.0 rationale).

Satisfaction signals:

  • Rapid security response (#12392 filed and merged same-day for RUSTSEC-2026-0486).
  • Contributor breadth in v0.9.0 (22 contributors) — healthy community.
  • Users are running ZeroClaw in production and filing precise, evidence-backed reports (grep proofs, revision hashes, reproduction steps) — a sign of an engaged, sophisticated user base rather than churn.

Net: High engagement, but a consistent theme of "the agent hides why things failed" across shell, cron, and trace subsystems — a coherent reliability narrative the maintainers should treat as a single workstream.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention:

  1. Issue #7461 — CI Windows/macOS test matrix (open since 2026-06-10, ~5 months, 6 comments, status:in-progress) https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7461 Accepted and in-progress but visibly stalled — platform regressions will keep slipping through until this lands.

  2. PR #9809 — Multiple models per provider profile (open since 2026-08-07, XL, schema-v4 redesign, 40+ labels) https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9809 A large architectural change with no merge in sight; risk of bit-rot against master.

  3. PR #10391 — Bounded delegate workspace/tool-ceiling/command-policy fix (#9872) (open since 2026-08-26, XL, risk:high) https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10391 Security-boundary correctness for delegates; long review cycle with repeated master merges — needs reviewer bandwidth.

  4. Issue #9814 + PR #11847 — Native XMPP (issue since Aug, PR since Oct 19, needs-maintainer-review, risk:high) https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/9814 · https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11847 Demand and implementation both exist; blocked on review. A decision (merge, split, or park explicitly) would help contributors.

  5. PR #11589 — Operator override for exceeded cost limit (open since Oct 7, needs-author-action) https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11589 Currently the only escape from an exceeded cost limit is a daemon restart — an operational sharp edge.

  6. Bulk of the 45 open PRs carry needs-author-action or needs-maintainer-review — a systematic review-capacity bottleneck rather than isolated neglect.

Health Verdict

Positive: Active contributor base, fast security patching, a substantive v0.9.0 with multi-user auth, and a sophisticated user community filing high-quality reports. Watch: 45 open PRs vs. 4 closed in 24h; zero fix PRs for today's four bugs (two S1/S2); and several XL/high-risk PRs aging past the two-month mark. The project's main risk is review throughput, not direction.
