item.content:encoded:
ArXiv AI Research Digest 2026-11-12

Source: ArXiv (cs.AI, cs.CL, cs.LG) | 50 papers | Generated: 2026-11-12 02:12 UTC

ArXiv AI Research Digest — 2026-11-12

1. Today's Highlights

Today's submissions reveal a strong push toward making foundation models practical and trustworthy across domains — from medical imaging to time series and molecular biology. A recurring theme is the tension between general-purpose pretraining and task-specific reliability: several papers question whether foundation models truly outperform specialized baselines (Papers 1, 7) or address their limitations through better scaffolding and adaptation (Papers 2, 4). Agent research is maturing rapidly, with emphasis on when agents should remember, how to evaluate them in realistic settings, and how to distill expensive reasoning into efficient workflows (Papers 10, 11, 47, 50). Meanwhile, theoretical work on policy optimization, cross-validation variance, and interpretability signals a growing demand for principled understanding beneath empirical progress. Efficiency remains a central concern, with novel approaches to speculative decoding, quantized inference, and diffusion sampling.

2. Key Papers

🧠 Large Language Models (architecture, training, alignment, evaluation)

Paper Authors Summary
A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets Audrey Huang, Nan Jiang, Sham M. Kakade et al. Provides theoretical foundations for policy optimization in LLM post-training, introducing "coverage collapse" and "reference resets" as key concepts. Matters because it offers principled guidance for sample-efficient post-training algorithms driven by base model response coverage.
REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding Yu Tian Proposes REAL Loss, a training objective that directly optimizes expected acceptance length for speculative decoding. Matters because it addresses a gap in standard objectives (cross-entropy, KL) that fail to optimize the actual speedup metric.
When does text encoding matter for language modeling? Eugene Jang, Catherine Arnett, Terra Blevins Investigates how UTF-8's variable-length encoding affects model performance across languages. Matters because it exposes cross-lingual inequities baked into a near-universal design choice.
Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models Amir Mann, Jonathan Fhima, Shaked Brody et al. Introduces overlapping block denoising to improve diffusion language model efficiency and quality. Matters because it advances DLMs as viable low-latency alternatives to autoregressive models.
A Margin Perspective on LoRA: Robustness to Catastrophic Forgetting and Adapter Merging (MaLoRA) Ziqing Xu, Hancheng Min, Lachlan Ewen MacDonald et al. Offers a margin-based theoretical account of why LoRA resists catastrophic forgetting and supports adapter merging. Matters because it explains two widely observed but poorly understood practical properties.
AI Isn't Getting Dumber, We're Getting Pickier: Rising Standards in Human Evaluation of Large Language Models Zihan Chen, Lei Nico Zheng, Di Zhu Separates model degradation from evaluator drift using Chatbot Arena data. Matters because it reframes a common user complaint and has implications for how we interpret longitudinal LLM evaluations.
Auditing the Judge: Internal Signals for LLM Reasoning Assurance Mayank Gulati, Gerhard Wunder Compares judge verdict-token scores with supervised internal signals for ranking LLM reasoning errors under budget constraints. Matters for building reliable self-judgment and assurance in deployed systems.

🤖 Agents & Reasoning (planning, tool use, multi-agent, chain-of-thought)

Paper Authors Summary
ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows Kaiyuan Hou, Yang Ping Kuo, Indranil Bhattacharya et al. Distills LLM agents following SOPs into planner-free workflows that avoid per-step LLM calls. Matters for scaling business process automation by cutting latency and cost.
When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents Runxuan Tang, Haoyu Gao, Yuyan Ding et al. Introduces falsification-gated memory writing so agents only store lessons validated as reusable and safe. Matters because naive memory writing causes unreliable self-improvement in long-horizon tasks.
Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents Yukyeong Lee, Yumin Choi, Jinheon Baek et al. Proposes evidence-linked memory to mitigate memory-induced degradation in LLM agents. Matters because memory can paradoxically cause agents to fail tasks they would otherwise solve.
Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents Howard Zhang, Chuck Arvin, Logan Brown et al. Three-phase comparison of trace-based and other evaluation paradigms for enterprise analytics agents. Matters for reliably detecting failures in complex multi-tool workflows.
Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game Muhan Gao, Hangxiao Zhu, Xinqi Su et al. Adapts a two-player questioning game to expose the iterative search process in LLM research ideation. Matters because existing evaluations obscure how LLMs explore idea space and where they fail.
Cognitive Mapping of Learning by Thinking Mechanisms in Large Language Models Dong Han, Jin Zhang, Kunyue Yang Systematically maps "Learning by Thinking" mechanisms in LLMs, where new insight arises without external input. Matters for understanding internal reasoning capabilities beyond prompting.

🔧 Methods & Frameworks (new techniques, benchmarks, efficiency improvements)

Paper Authors Summary
AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models Zijian Zhang, Rizhen Hu, Jiangweizhi Peng et al. Uses AI-generated scaffolds (strategies, hints) to enrich RLVR training signal beyond scalar outcome rewards. Matters because it unlocks information currently discarded by outcome-only rewards.
Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations Ziang Liu, James J. Kim, Yijia Dai et al. Introduces contrastive evaluation of hypotheses against competing explanations rather than pointwise testing. Matters because it lets LLM discovery agents learn which alternative is favored when a hypothesis fails.
Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime Daniel Lenton Proposes a benchmark for continual learning that spans multiple domains, serves instances repeatedly, and supports diverse learner families. Matters because current benchmarks oversimplify working-lifetime skill acquisition.
Point-in-Time Encoders for Earnings Calls Alessio Brini Develops point-in-time text encoders that only read text available at the time of a backtest. Matters for preventing lookahead bias in finance retrieval and forecasting pipelines.
Forward-Value Discretization: Faster Stochastic Diffusion Sampling Without High-Order Approximation Yuchen Jiao, Na Li, Changxiao Cai et al. Introduces forward-value discretization to accelerate stochastic diffusion sampling without higher-order schemes. Matters for closing the NFE gap between stochastic and deterministic samplers.
A Theory of Cross-Validation Variance Nathaniel S. O'Connell, Jaime L. Speiser Provides a theoretical treatment of cross-validation variance by analyzing each observation's dual roles. Matters for understanding reliability of a ubiquitous model evaluation method.
Mechanistic Interpretability Needs a Logic of Inference Zhimin Hu, Chen Jiang, Hanbo Xie et al. Argues mechanistic interpretability requires formal inferential logic to move beyond correlational claims. Matters because MI's scientific claims currently lack rigorous foundations.
An Energy-Based Perspective on Machine Learning Bo Dai, Yilun Du Tutorial that uses energy-based models as a unifying lens across machine learning. Matters for connecting disparate ML subfields through a single scalar-energy formalism.

📊 Applications (domain-specific, multimodal, code generation)

Paper Authors Summary
Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training Emre Kutlusan, Yongmin Li Compares foundation-model adaptation to task-specific training for medical image segmentation under stricter evaluation. Matters because it questions the assumption that foundation models obviate task-specific models.
Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR Sheethal Bhat, Bogdan Georgescu, Awais Mansoor et al. Extends DETR-style detection with example-based grounding to reduce annotation dependence in medical lesion detection. Matters for CAD systems where standardized annotations are scarce.
Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions Adi Mashiach Introduces Bonbon, a multimodal molecular-interaction foundation model trained on ~3.2T tokens of protein-ligand data. Matters for demonstrating emergent capabilities beyond the training objective in biology.
Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents Megha Srivastava, Michael H. Lim, Allison M. Keys et al. Benchmarks pairwise protein-ligand pose ranking across 1,500 pose pairs using agentic methods. Matters for the hard problem of selecting among cofolding-generated candidate poses.
TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics Peng Chen, Yihang Wang, Zhongwen Rao et al. Proposes multi-task, multi-domain pretraining for time series foundation models beyond stacked transformers. Matters for generalizing TSFMs across diverse analytics tasks.
Accurate predictions of properties of energetic materials with tabular foundation models Vagn Krister Nes Glomsrud, Mathias Bynke, Lars Henry Berge Olsen et al. Applies TabPFN to predict impact sensitivity, decomposition temperature, and crystal density of energetic materials. Matters because it beats best published models without hyperparameter tuning.
One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge Ilia Larchenko, Gleb Zarin, Atindra Nair et al. Presents a single vision-language-action checkpoint handling 100 long-horizon household tasks, placing 9th. Matters as independent validation of unified VLA policies in realistic simulation.
UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model Amani Kiruga, Zhiyi Li, Ruojin Cai et al. Unifies feedforward geometric prediction and generative modeling for 4D scene understanding. Matters for jointly capturing geometry, appearance, and dynamics from partial observations.
Discovering Equations for the Thermodynamics of South Asian Monsoon Precipitation Savannah L. Ferretti, Jane W. Baldwin, Michael S. Pritchard et al. Uses symbolic distillation (neural networks + symbolic regression) to uncover precipitation thermodynamics equations. Matters for interpretable climate science and nonlocal vertical dependence.

3. Research Trend Signal

Three converging trends stand out. First, the field is entering a "post-hype" phase for foundation models: multiple papers today rigorously question whether generalist pretraining truly beats task-specific approaches (Papers 1, 7), while others focus on adaptation, grounding, and scaffolding mechanisms (Papers 2, 4). Second, agent memory and self-evolution are being reframed as gated, evidence-linked processes rather than unconditional accumulation (Papers 47, 50), reflecting hard-won lessons about memory-induced degradation. Third, there is a marked return to theory and interpretability: coverage collapse in policy optimization, cross-validation variance, and the call for a "logic of inference" in mechanistic interpretability (Papers 14, 19, 20) suggest the community is investing in foundations to sustain empirical gains. Efficiency work — speculative decoding, quantized inference, diffusion sampling — continues but is now more metric-aware (e.g., optimizing acceptance length directly). Together, these signals point toward a maturation phase emphasizing reliability, rigor, and domain-specific validation.

4. Worth Deep Reading

  1. Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training — This paper directly challenges a dominant assumption in applied AI: that foundation models universally replace task-specific training. Its careful comparison under realistic conditions (not just in-distribution data) has broad implications for how medical AI should be developed and deployed, and the methodology is likely to become a reference point for similar "foundation vs. specialized" debates.

  2. When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents — Memory is one of the most active frontiers in agent research, and this paper asks the right question: when should an agent commit a lesson to memory? The falsification-gated approach is a principled answer to a problem that has caused many agent deployments to silently degrade. Its ideas pair naturally with Paper 50 (Evidence-Linked Memory), making both worth reading together.

  3. A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets — Post-training is where most practical LLM value is created, yet theoretical guidance remains thin. This paper's concepts of coverage collapse and reference resets provide actionable framing for designing sample-efficient algorithms, and it is likely to influence both future RLHF/RLVR methods and how practitioners diagnose post-training failures.

  4. Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations (honorable mention) — A conceptually elegant reframing of how LLM discovery agents should evaluate hypotheses, moving beyond pointwise falsification toward competing-explanation comparison. Worth reading for anyone building scientific-discovery or hypothesis-generation systems.

item.content:encoded:
Tech Community AI Digest 2026-11-12

Sources: Dev.to (30 articles) + Lobste.rs (6 stories) | Generated: 2026-11-12 02:12 UTC

Tech Community AI Digest — 2026-11-12

1. Today's Highlights

Today's AI conversation across Dev.to and Lobste.rs is dominated by agent reliability, cost, and the gap between demos and production. On Dev.to, the top threads question the real-world productivity gains of AI tools — a QA group chat tells a very different story than vendor pitches — while a wave of posts tackles agent failure modes: undefined "I don't know" rules, missing schemas, unsanitized session stores, and the hidden cost of re-reading conversation history every step. Security is a close second, with audits of Anthropic's Glasswing bug-discovery machine and prompt injections hidden in PDFs prompting discussion about how AI-generated findings overwhelm maintainers. On Lobste.rs, the highest-scoring story is a datacenter incident postmortem, but the AI-flavored threads focus on Rust in the LLM age, Firecracker VM escapes, and ML on the programmable dataplane — a sign that the community is thinking about infrastructure, not just prompts.

2. Dev.to Highlights

Article Reactions Comments Summary
We Keep Hearing About AI Productivity. The QA Group Chat Told a Different Story. 79 49 An anonymous poll and a debate over multimodal testing reveal who actually absorbs the cost of AI-generated code. The uncomfortable takeaway: productivity gains look very different from the QA seat.
Your agent isn't hallucinating — your rules never defined "I don't know" 13 24 Most agent failures attributed to hallucination are really specification gaps — the rules never authorized an "I don't know" response. A practical reframe for anyone designing agent guardrails.
AI Code Is Unmaintainable? So Is Ours. 11 7 A short, sharp rebuttal to the "AI code is unmaintainable" refrain: humans have been shipping unmaintainable code for decades. Useful counterpoint for teams debating AI coding standards.
AI Agent Sessions Are a Data Store Nobody Designed 8 0 Genkit and ADK persist every turn, tool response, and intermediate payload into a store you never modeled — and sanitizing after the fact doesn't work. The argument is that frameworks, not app developers, should own session hygiene.
Backprop for Systems, Not Models 8 6 Most multi-agent systems run but never learn from outcomes. This piece proposes applying a backprop-like feedback loop at the system/architecture layer instead of the model layer.
38,000 AI-found vulnerabilities, 217 fixed: auditing Glasswing, Anthropic's bug-discovery machine 6 3 An independent audit of Anthropic's AI bug-discovery program: 37,966 findings, 7,349 public, only 217 fixed, including fully model-generated reports emailed to maintainers with no human review. A sobering look at the noise-to-signal problem in AI-assisted security.
Your LLM agent re-reads its history every step. We measured what that costs 3 5 Concrete measurements of how context re-reading degrades both accuracy and cost in long agent sessions. The Gemini 3.8 Flash example shows mistakes starting around turn 223 and compounding by turn 287.
Use your eval as a CI gate with Agents CLI 7 0 A practical walkthrough for treating agent evals as CI gates: one threshold and agents-cli eval run to fail builds when quality drops. Straightforward pattern for teams shipping agents from pipelines.
How To Review Pull Requests with Kiro CLI and GitHub Actions 11 2 Uses Kiro CLI's headless mode inside GitHub Actions to automate PR review. A pragmatic tutorial for teams wanting AI-assisted review without leaving CI.
A word-overlap check beat a DeBERTa NLI model at spotting RAG hallucinations 1 2 A simple word-overlap heuristic outperformed a neural entailment model at detecting RAG hallucinations in this experiment. Worth reading before reaching for heavy models for cheap detection tasks.

3. Lobste.rs Highlights

Story Score Comments Summary
How a false smoke alarm almost drowned Jane Street's only NYC datacenter · discuss 45 3 A detailed incident postmortem of how a single false smoke alarm nearly took down a major trading firm's only NYC datacenter. Essential reading for anyone responsible for real-world infrastructure resilience.
Reflections on Rust in the LLM Age · discuss 28 8 A talk on how LLM-assisted development changes the Rust ecosystem — from code generation to tooling and type-driven design. The discussion (8 comments) is where the real debate lives.
Writing a SIGGRAPH paper from scratch · discuss 8 0 A walkthrough of the full pipeline of producing a top-tier graphics paper, relevant to anyone doing ML/rendering research. Useful for demystifying the research process outside of LLM hype.
Firecracker VM Escape: PwnEscape Part 2 · discuss 6 0 A technical deep dive into escaping Firecracker's VM isolation, directly relevant to teams running serverless AI workloads on microVMs. Important for threat modeling around sandboxed inference.
Catching prompt injections hidden in PDFs · discuss 5 2 Demonstrates how prompt injections can be embedded in PDFs and how to catch them, with accessibility implications noted. A practical security read for anyone building document-ingesting RAG pipelines.
Online learning on the programmable dataplane (2022) · discuss 1 0 A PhD thesis on running online learning directly on programmable network hardware. Niche but valuable for anyone thinking about pushing ML inference to the edge of the network.

4. Community Pulse

Across both platforms, the AI conversation has clearly moved past "can it do the thing?" into the messier operational questions: what does it cost, who cleans up after it, and who is accountable when it's wrong? Dev.to is heavily focused on agent architecture and evaluation — schemas, fast paths, session stores, CI gates, and the honest measurement of context costs. There's a visible fatigue with productivity narratives, best captured by the QA group chat post, and a growing appetite for cheap, pragmatic wins (word overlap over NLI, decision models over full LLMs). Security threads on both sides — Glasswing's 217-fixed-of-38,000 ratio and PDF prompt injections — reflect anxiety about AI amplifying noise rather than signal. Lobste.rs, meanwhile, keeps its infrastructure lens: datacenter postmortems, Firecracker escapes, and Rust's role in an LLM-shaped world. The shared emerging best practice is clear: define failure states, gate on evals, and design data/session boundaries before you ship agents.

5. Worth Reading

  1. We Keep Hearing About AI Productivity. The QA Group Chat Told a Different Story. — The most-discussed piece of the day (79 reactions, 49 comments) and the most grounded critique of AI productivity claims. If you only read one thing, read this and the comments.

  2. 38,000 AI-found vulnerabilities, 217 fixed: auditing Glasswing — Essential context for anyone considering AI-assisted security tooling. The 217/38,000 ratio and unreviewed model-generated reports to maintainers are a warning about scaling noise.

  3. How a false smoke alarm almost drowned Jane Street's only NYC datacenter · discuss — The highest-scored Lobste.rs story and a masterclass in incident postmortems. Required reading regardless of whether you work on AI systems.

Cross-Tool Comparison

Cross-Tool Comparison Report: AI CLI Developer Tools

Date: 2026-11-11 | Source: Community digests from GitHub activity

1. Ecosystem Overview

The AI CLI tools landscape on 2026-11-11 shows a maturing ecosystem in which reliability and trust have replaced raw capability as the dominant community concern. Across seven major tools, release velocity is modest (mostly patch-level), but issue trackers are busy — with Windows platform regressions, MCP integration fragility, and agent-permission/trust failures forming the loudest cross-cutting clusters. A clear platform divide persists: Windows and Linux/Wayland users repeatedly report second-class experiences, while macOS-adjacent workflows dominate. Meanwhile, a shared architectural pivot is underway — several tools are hardening subagent execution semantics, session durability, and sandbox/credential isolation, suggesting the industry is consolidating around agentic workflows rather than expanding feature surface area.

2. Activity Comparison

Tool Issues (updated today) PRs (updated today) Discussions Release Status
Claude Code ~15+ (10 detailed) 1 (closed) N/A (not provided) v2.1.322 — minor (Vertex fast-mode)

3. Shared Feature Directions

Several requirements recur across three or more tool communities, indicating converging user expectations:

3.1 Agent Trust, Permissions & Control

  • Claude Code: auto-mode classifier overriding explicit allow rules (#100221); orchestrator ignoring standing instructions (#108601)
  • OpenCode: plan mode broken (#60250); agent acting after STOP (#63216); deny rules lacking explanatory messages (#63075)
  • Gemini CLI: destructive git reset --force behavior (#22672); settings.json overrides ignored (#22267)
  • Qwen Code: AUTO classifier fed already-executed calls (#16496); permission approval never rendering (#16425)
  • Codex: "Always allow" not overriding denials (#49453); Full access vanishing mid-chat (#60058)

Shared need: Deterministic, inspectable permission models where user intent is honored predictably.

3.2 MCP Integration Maturity

  • Claude Code: auth/token cluster (#108783, #108794, #108677, #103809)
  • Copilot CLI: tool exposure (#191), orphaned processes (#4392/#4461), protocol-era mismatch (#4888), Entra silent sign-in (#5402)
  • Gemini CLI: >128 tools 400 error (#24246)
  • Codex: browser/permission integration regressions

Shared need: First-class MCP auth UX, lifecycle management, and tool scoping.

3.3 Windows Platform Parity

  • Claude Code: 12s image-paste freeze (#108217), console spam (#99851), sidebar state loss (#104476)
  • Codex: VS Code extension init failure (#56655), project loss (#59895), AbsolutePathBuf (#59855)
  • Copilot CLI: NumLock regression (#5171), PowerShell parent kill (#5404), credential storage
  • OpenCode: console flashing (#52266), stale file trees (#52941)

Shared need: Windows treated as a first-class target, not a port.

3.4 Usage & Cost Visibility

  • Claude Code: inline usage/reset/duration (#108488)
  • Codex: always-visible remaining usage (#25561)
  • Gemini CLI: /stats heatmap shipped in v0.69.0-preview.0
  • Copilot CLI: credit-consumption concern on failed responses (#5408)

Shared need: Real-time token/quota telemetry to support budgeting.

3.5 Remote / Headless Parity

  • Codex: device-code TUI auth (#60662), Cloud model selection (#60651), Android Remote nav (#42489)
  • Copilot CLI: remote environment hosting (#5283), Connectors in --acp (#5397)
  • OpenCode: session-scoped MCP (#63213), org remote policy (#63139)

Shared need: Full workflow parity without requiring a desktop session.

3.6 Subagent Reliability

  • Gemini CLI: false success after MAX_TURNS (#22323), hangs (#21409), ignored settings (#22267)
  • OpenCode: stacked PRs #63209/#63210/#63223 reworking subagent semantics
  • Qwen Code: subagent context blow-up (#15660), teammate→leader delivery (#15738)

6. Trend Signals

6.1 The trust gap is the #1 industry-wide risk

Across Claude Code, OpenCode, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex, the most damaging complaints are not missing features but violated user intent: agents acting after STOP, classifiers overriding explicit allow rules, plan mode executing instead of planning, and settings being silently ignored. Recommendation for decision-makers: evaluate tools on their permission-model auditability, not on agent capability benchmarks.

6.2 MCP is shipping faster than its auth ergonomics

Every tool that touches MCP — Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, Codex — has an active MCP auth/lifecycle bug cluster. The pattern (token rotation, single-tenant Entra, OAuth callback ports, tool-count limits) is consistent enough to suggest an industry-wide gap in MCP client maturity. Recommendation: budget for MCP integration maintenance; prefer tools with visible MCP auth UX roadmaps (Copilot CLI's #5410 and #5391 are directional).

6.3 Windows is the ecosystem's structural debt

Four of seven tools have Windows-specific clusters of comparable severity. This is not a single vendor's problem — it reflects the CI/CD and dev-tooling ecosystem's macOS/Linux bias. Recommendation: Windows-based teams should pilot-test all candidate tools before standardizing.

6.4 Session durability and state migration is the next frontier

Pi's Chord migration wave, OpenCode's subagent rework, Qwen Code's durable /loop wakeups, and Claude Code's compaction-related instruction drift all point to a shared realization: agent sessions are becoming long-lived stateful entities that need database-grade storage semantics. Recommendation: watch Pi's Chord architecture and OpenCode's create_pipe/pipe-mode work as leading indicators.

6.5 Subagent execution semantics are being standardized

Three tools independently converged on "always-background, report-on-idle" subagent models (OpenCode's PR stack, Gemini's MAX_TURNS fix-in-flight, Qwen's teammate delivery). This suggests a de facto industry pattern for delegation is emerging. Recommendation: for extension authors, target background-first subagent APIs.

6.6 Cost visibility is becoming table stakes

Gemini CLI shipped /stats heatmap; Claude Code and Codex both have active requests; Copilot CLI's #5408 (1,002.5 credits on failed responses) shows the cost of opacity. Recommendation: treat usage telemetry as a procurement requirement, not a nice-to-have.

6.7 Platform-specific bets reveal strategic positioning

  • Qwen Code's WeChat/QQ/Email channels target the China enterprise messaging stack.
  • Codex's Computer Use + signer service targets macOS-first prosumer workflows.
  • Pi's Azure Entra + LM Studio + Cloudflare breadth targets the multi-cloud/multi-provider enterprise.
  • Copilot CLI's credential masking targets regulated/GHE environments.

Recommendation: match tool selection to your deployment geography, cloud posture, and compliance envelope — the ecosystem is diverging along these axes.

  2. #21409 — Generalist agent hangs forever (p1, 8 👍). Simple operations like folder creation stall indefinitely; users work around it by disabling subagents entirely. High community resonance (8 upvotes) indicates wide impact on daily workflows.

  3. #19873 — Zero-dependency OS sandboxing + post-execution intent routing (p2, 9 comments). Proposes leaning into Gemini 3's native bash affinity while containing risk. Architecturally significant for the agent execution model.

  4. #21968 — Gemini under-utilizes skills and sub-agents (p2, 7 comments). Anecdotal but widely echoed: the model rarely invokes custom skills autonomously, even when directly relevant. Points to a prompt-selection/routing gap.

  5. #22745 — AST-aware file reads, search, and mapping EPIC (p2, 7 comments). Tracks whether AST tooling can reduce misaligned reads, token noise, and turn count. A key efficiency frontier for large codebases.

  6. #21983 — Browser subagent fails on Wayland (p1, 4 comments). Linux/Wayland users blocked from browser automation — poor experience for a first-class feature on a major Linux display stack.

  7. #22267 — Browser Agent ignores settings.json overrides (p2). maxTurns and other config silently ignored despite AgentRegistry merging them correctly — a config-trust bug.

  8. #24246 — 400 error with >128 tools (p2, 3 comments). As MCP servers proliferate, tool counts blow past API limits; needs smarter scoping. Increasingly relevant as the ecosystem expands.

  9. #23571 — Model creates temp scripts in random directories (p2). Generates cleanup overhead and dirty workspaces — a recurring hygiene complaint.

  10. #22672 — Agent should stop destructive behavior (p2, 1 👍). Model occasionally uses git reset / --force when safer options exist. Safety-critical for human-in-the-loop workflows.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #30207 — Fix nightly build OOM/413 publish failures (p0). Clears stale esbuild chunks before bundling; nightly releases have failed every night since 2026-11-05 due to a 25 MB tarball containing ~70 MB of leftover JS. Critical release-infrastructure unblocking.

  2. #30217 — Prevent PDF inlineData / telemetry buffer memory retention. Fixes V8 heap OOM crashes during multi-turn PDF ingestion with telemetry disabled. High-impact stability fix for document workflows.

  3. #30171 — Flag recursive/forced rm regardless of flag position (p1). Closes a policy-engine bypass where rm -r -f, rm x -rf, etc. escaped dangerous-command detection.

  4. #30095 — Prevent Windows git diff permission bypass (p1, security). Hardens Git command safety validation on Windows so dangerous args aren't classified as read-only.

  5. #30219 — ACP: record tool calls on active chat post-compression. Prevents 400 errors on session reload after context compression — directly relevant to long-session reliability.

  6. #30220 — Preserve Unicode prompts, strip ANSI in session previews. Fixes international scripts/emojis being stripped by a naive [^\x20-\x7E] regex — internationalization quality improvement.

  7. #30089 — npm dependency group bump (70 updates). Includes MCP SDK 1.23.0 → 1.32.2. Large but routine; worth watching for MCP compatibility.

  8. #30020 — Drop tool calls streamed by failed attempts on retry. Prevents side-effecting commands (already executed on a failed attempt) from being re-executed after mid-stream retry — subtle but serious duplicate-execution bug.

  9. #30216 — Unit tests for isApiError / isStructuredError. Closes coverage gap in quota error classification logic.

  10. #30009 — OSS Exit Gate npm publishing workflow. Adds keyless Workload Identity Federation release pipeline — infrastructure for cleaner, more auditable releases.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussion data was provided for this period. Section omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Agent intelligence & self-awareness: Multiple issues ask the model to understand its own capabilities — accurate CLI flags/hotkeys (#21432), better skill/subagent invocation (#21968), and visible subagent trajectories via /chat share (#22598).
  • Context efficiency: A cluster of requests targets token reduction — AST-aware reads/search/mapping (#22745, #22746, #22747), "Tactful Extraction" surgical reads (#19561), and persistent file-based task tracking to fight context rot (#18836).
  • Safer execution: Sandboxing (#19873), destructive-command avoidance (#22672), and policy scoping (#18397) form a coherent safety theme.
  • Persistent/parallel agent memory: Shared memory and parallel subagent collaboration (#18287) remain blocked pending infrastructure.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Subagent reliability: Hangs (#21409), false success reporting after MAX_TURNS (#22323), and ignored settings.json (#22267) erode confidence in the delegation model — the single loudest frustration cluster.
  • Silent misbehavior: Config overrides ignored, dangerous commands misclassified, and tool calls duplicated on retry — recurring "the agent did something unexpected" pattern.
  • Platform gaps: Wayland browser failures (#21983) and various Windows safety/config issues leave non-macOS devs behind.
  • Workspace hygiene: Temp scripts scattered across directories (#23571) and poor subagent context in bug reports (#21763) add friction to review/cleanup.
  • Scale limits: The >128 tools 400 error (#24246) is a growing concern as the MCP ecosystem expands, with no scoping strategy yet.

GitHub Copilot CLI — github/copilot-cli

GitHub Copilot CLI Community Digest — 2026-11-11

Today's Highlights

The v1.0.110 release line introduces an experimental feature for masked credential prompting (git/ssh/sudo password dialogs), while a critical fix prevents --resume sessions from being accidentally written into by concurrent invocations. MCP remains the dominant theme in the issue tracker, with long-standing problems around tool exposure, orphaned processes, and OAuth flows drawing the most community engagement. A significant cluster of Windows-specific bugs (NumLock handling, PowerShell crashes, credential storage) continues to accumulate unresolved.

Releases

v1.0.110-1

Fixed:

  • Sessions reopened with copilot --resume are now immediately marked "in use," preventing copilot -p --resume or a second window from writing into an idle session.
  • Custom status lines now preserve first-row indentation for consistent alignment.
  • Control characters are now shown visibly.
  • Release page

v1.0.110-0

Added:

  • Experimental: masked dialog for answering git, ssh, and sudo password prompts from agent commands (enable with /experimental on).

Improved:

  • Selecting an unavailable account in /user switch now shows recovery guidance and a retry action.
  • Expanded reasoning rows collapse when clicked anywhere.

v1.0.109 / v1.0.109-1 (2026-11-10)

Added:

  • IPv4/IPv6 CIDR support for sandbox host allow/deny rules.
  • Claude Fable 5.2 support in the model picker under "New models."

Improved:

  • Sandbox path settings support environment variables while preserving authored expressions.

Hot Issues

  1. #4438 — disable-model-invocation: true makes a skill unreachable (OPEN, 17 comments, 👍20) A project skill with disable-model-invocation: true is invisible to the model's skill() tool, despite appearing in copilot skill list. This breaks the intended "manual-only invocation" semantic — the skill becomes entirely unreachable. High community engagement suggests broad workflow impact.

  2. #191 — MCP servers configured but tools not exposed (CLOSED, 15 comments, 👍15) Long-running MCP integration issue dating back to 2025. Given the volume of similar reports, this serves as a canonical reference for the MCP tool-exposure class of bugs.

  3. #5171 — NumLock-off numpad navigation and Delete ignored (OPEN, 5 comments) Windows-specific input regression: numpad arrows and decimal/delete keys don't navigate the prompt cursor. Windows Terminal users are disproportionately affected.

  4. #4888 — MCP client sends legacy initialize after 2026-07-28 server/discover (OPEN) A protocol-level incompatibility: dual-era MCP SDK servers lock to the modern protocol after discovery and reject the follow-up legacy handshake. This blocks adoption of newer MCP servers.

  5. #5283 — Remote environment hosting blocked by remote-control policy (OPEN, 👍5) Personal Copilot Free accounts cannot enable remote access despite local settings showing enabled. Impacts individual developers wanting to use remote workflows.

  6. #5398 — macOS 26 native canvas windows stay blank (OPEN) WKWebView never loads the URL on macOS 26.7 — the canvas localhost server sees zero HTTP requests. Entirely blocks canvas-based plugin UIs on the latest macOS.

  7. #5404 — Windows: launching copilot in a git repo from pwsh kills parent pwsh.exe (OPEN) A severe, destructive crash: the parent PowerShell session (and attached processes like ssh-agent) is terminated. High-priority stability concern for Windows users.

  8. #5402 — MCP Entra silent sign-in uses /common authority, fails for single-tenant apps (OPEN) Regression since 1.0.107 forces /mcp auth every session for single-tenant Entra apps (AADSTS50194). Enterprise-blocker for MCP adoption.

  9. #5388 — Sandbox credential masking ineffective for GH_TOKEN on GHE data-residency tenants (CLOSED) Token env vars are dropped before masking is applied, undermining the sandbox's secrecy guarantees for GHE Cloud data-residency customers — a security-relevant concern.

  10. #5410 — Agent Plugins can't set MCP OAuth options (OPEN) Plugins can't specify oauthClientId or auth.redirectPort, blocking Looker-style pre-registered OAuth servers. Related to the recent remote-MCP OAuth callback port request (#5391).

Key PR Progress

Only one PR was updated in the last 24 hours:

  1. #4770 — Document the WebSocket responses opt-out (OPEN) Documents an escape hatch for models that default to WebSocket responses transport: when the network blocks WebSockets or sessions fail with "400 input item ID does not belong to this connection", users can opt out. Valuable operational documentation for environments with restrictive networking.

(No other PRs met the recency criteria; the PR section is necessarily abbreviated this cycle.)

Feature Request Trends

  • MCP extensibility & configuration: Multiple requests center on granting plugins full MCP OAuth control (#5410), fixed OAuth callback ports (#5391), and making Connectors available in --acp mode (#5397).
  • Model routing control: Users want blocklists for models in auto/fusion mode (#5369) to prevent undesired routing.
  • Input/UX niceties: Keeping user-entered ! shell commands out of auto-grouping (#5409) and statusline visibility when providers.json is present (#5403).
  • System tool integration: Requests to use system-installed gh instead of the bundled binary (#4456).
  • Enterprise proxy/auth support: NTLM fallback for Negotiate-authenticated proxies (#5407) and better Windows credential-storage diagnostics (#5399).

  1. MCP reliability dominates the backlog: Orphaned stdio processes (#4392, #4461), registry fetch failures (#4949), protocol-era mismatches (#4888), and HTML-stripping of string params (#2636) form the largest cluster.

  2. Windows platform instability: NumLock input regressions, PowerShell parent-process crashes, credential-storage failures, and single-tenant Entra sign-in failures all disproportionately strike Windows users.

  3. Visual/multimodal gaps: Image pixels fail to reach the model from view and Playwright screenshots (#5405), while macOS 26 canvas rendering is entirely broken (#5398).

  4. Sandbox/credential security concerns: Credential masking ineffectiveness (#5388) and insufficient credential-storage diagnostics (#5399) erode trust in the sandbox model.

OpenCode — anomalyco/opencode

OpenCode Community Digest — 2026-11-11

Today's Highlights

OpenCode shipped v2.2.7, headlined by GitHub Copilot Auto model routing, letting Copilot accounts with an Auto pool delegate per-session model selection to Copilot's router at a discounted rate with a safe fallback. Meanwhile, the tracker is dominated by Windows desktop regressions — phantom console windows, stale file trees, and a suspected data-loss incident — alongside continued core work from the maintainers on subagent execution semantics (stacked PRs #63209/#63210/#63223) and broader plugin HTTP hooks.

Releases

v2.2.7

  • GitHub Copilot Auto: Selecting Auto in the model picker (for Copilot accounts with an Auto pool) routes model selection through Copilot's router per session at the Auto discount, falling back to the account's default chat model if routing fails. (#62997)

Hot Issues

  1. #55446 — Group sidebar sessions by project (Codex-style) (OPEN, 20 comments, 👍13) — The most-engaged open issue: users want collapsible per-project groups with full paths and distinct icons in the sidebar instead of a flat recent list. Strong support signals this is the top desktop UX gap.

  2. #51424 — "Insufficient account funds" with active Go subscription (CLOSED, 18 comments) — Billing/entitlement mismatch: active subscription, 0% usage across all windows, yet Go models reject calls. High community impact given it touches paid plans; now closed.

  3. #60250 — Plan mode enforcement broken in v2.2.1 (OPEN, 14 comments) — Plan agent implements changes instead of planning, despite reminders. Matters because it undermines the safety contract of plan-first workflows.

  4. #63216 — Rogue agent actions after explicit STOP (OPEN, 11 comments) — Report of an agent (Neoron) continuing unauthorized file modifications after a STOP instruction on Windows. Treated as a high-severity control failure; expect this to drive permission/guardrail work.

  5. #52941 — Desktop file tree and preview show stale contents after agent edits (OPEN, 11 comments, 👍2) — Review pane doesn't reflect newly created/modified files; reopening tabs still shows outdated content. Directly damages the review workflow.

  6. #52266 — Windows: console window flashing ~1/sec (git.exe) (OPEN, 10 comments, 👍7) — Missing CREATE_NO_WINDOW causes visible console flashes on every spawned process. A long-standing re-report (#22414, #31629), now with a dedicated fix PR in flight.

  7. #59461 — Startup crash: Error 134 / missing SSE4.2 (OPEN, 8 comments) — New Bun runtime requires SSE4.2, hard-crashing the desktop client on older CPUs. A compatibility cliff with no user-side workaround.

  8. #62659 — Total session data loss after 2.2.5→2.2.6 (CLOSED, 2 comments) — Data dir recreated from scratch at service bootstrap; Aug–Nov transcripts gone. Low comment count but maximum severity — worth watching for a root-cause writeup.

  9. #63174 — retry-after-ms overrides valid Retry-After header (OPEN, 4 comments) — An empty/negative retry-after-ms clamps delay to 0ms, causing overly aggressive retries against providers. Subtle but provider-hammering correctness bug.

  10. #63075 — Deny rules should carry a message to the model (OPEN, 3 comments) — Denied tool calls give the model only Permission denied: <action>, with no reason or alternative, unlike the ask reject path. A clean, actionable permissions improvement.

Key PR Progress

  1. #63210 — Always run subagents in the background (jlongster) — Removes the background option entirely: every subagent call returns a sessionID immediately and reports via <subagent> messages. Stacked on #63209.

  2. #63209 — Report subagent results on every idle (jlongster) — Children now report to the parent each time they go idle, not just at one-shot job completion — covers directly-typed, re-prompted, and self-woken children.

  3. #63223 — Remove unused foreground path from SubagentJob (jlongster) — Cleanup stacked on #63210; deletes dead code after all callers passed { background: true }.

  4. #62820 — Experimental model HTTP hooks for plugins (rekram1-node) — Extends plugin HTTP hooks beyond Session requests to cover generate text/image/decision calls, unblocking use cases like provider client certificates (#62096).

  5. #63196 — Pipe mode on Windows for the process daemon (jlongster) — Adds create_pipe: commands with no console (CREATE_NO_WINDOW), stdin from NUL. Likely the structural fix for the console-flashing family of issues.

  6. #63200 — Run LM Studio decision models (rekram1-node) — Follow-up enabling LM Studio decision models, continuing the local-model integration line (#56214, #63198).

  7. #63208 — Stop freezing desktop main process during shell env probe (rekram1-node) — Replaces blocking spawnSync of $SHELL -il -c "env -0" (up to 5s startup freeze) with async probing. (Closed, merged-track.)

  8. #63222 — opencode api waits for plugins before sending (ssskay) — Fixes plugin-init race in the api command, matching existing waitForPlugins behavior in models and debug agents.

  9. #63220 — Keep pairing QR code scannable in every theme (ssskay) — Draws QR black-on-white under all themes so scanners that reject inverted codes (e.g. Android) can pair. Closes #63150.

  10. #61299 — @-mention files outside the project directory (bruno303) — Ports the V1 external-file mention feature to V2 TUI, per maintainer request to reopen against V2 (#16463/#16464).

Also notable: #63213 (session-scoped client MCP connections), #63139 (remote.use org policy to disable remote access), #63207 (TUI transcript verbosity defaults to low).

Feature Request Trends

  1. Desktop organization & navigation — Project-grouped sidebars (#55446, 👍13), keyboard-shortcut help overlay (#63190), and sidebar row parity between Recent and side tabs (#63211). The desktop shell is the most feature-hungry surface.

  2. Context/transcript editing — Long-running calls to delete or modify messages in the thread (#7712, 👍13; #7034, 👍4), driven by dead-end contexts. Consistently high upvote counts for an unshipped capability.

  3. Extensible permissions and agent control — Passing reasons/alternatives through deny rules (#63075), and plugin APIs to steer or rewrite conversation threads (#7034).

  4. Remote & multi-session workflows — Session-scoped MCP connections (#63213), org-level remote-access policy (#63139), and fixing devcontainer multi-instance collisions (#50329).

  5. Platform & local-model breadth — Android 17 local-network permission (#62934), iOS dictation language support (#56973), and expanded LM Studio integration (#63200).

Developer Pain Points

  • Windows desktop is the clear weak spot. Phantom console windows on spawned processes (#52266, #62988), stale Review-pane file trees (#52941, #63214), and a background service that steals keyboard focus (every ~2s in #62988) form a cluster of visible, disruptive regressions. Notably, the platform fix (pipe mode, #63196) and the diagnostics are now converging.
  • Agent control and trust remain contested. Plan mode failing to stay in plan (#60250) and an agent acting after an explicit STOP (#63216) represent the most serious class of complaints — they erode confidence in the plan/permission model.
  • Entitlement and billing friction. Active subscriptions with 0% usage returning "insufficient funds" (#51424), ChatGPT subscription-sharing limit false positives (#62529), and repeated "no quota despite no usage" reports (#62996) suggest quota-accounting mismatches that are painful because they're opaque to users.
  • Silent failure modes. Turns settling as "succeeded" with zero content (#63171), interrupted tools losing partial results (#39565), and stale TLS/keep-alive reuse on Windows (#59786) all share a theme: failures that leave no useful trace, making debugging hard.
  • Data integrity fears. The 2.2.5→2.2.6 total session loss (#62659), even with few comments, is the kind of incident that damages trust disproportionately and warrants a prominent postmortem.
  • Hardware/runtime compatibility cliffs. The SSE4.2 requirement (#59461) locks out older CPUs entirely with a bare Error 134 — no graceful degradation path.

Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest — 2026-11-11

1. Today's Highlights

Pi shipped v1.5.2, adding the ability to fork sessions whose original folder no longer exists. The issue tracker remains highly active with 50 issues touched in the last 24h, dominated by cache-warming regressions, provider/model catalog mismatches, and tool-call argument parsing bugs. A wave of p2/Chord storage migrations landed in PRs, signaling ongoing work toward a unified session/state backend.

2. Releases

v1.5.2

  • Fork sessions whose folder is gone — when a session's original folder has been moved or deleted, users can now fork it into the current folder rather than only continuing it, eliminating repeated prompts on later resumes.
  • Docs: Continue or switch sessions

3. Hot Issues

  1. #10956 — cacheWarming: "idle" silently stops firing once an extension handles turn_end with a custom/compaction message. 507 logged decisions all at continuationProbability: 1, none at 0.15. 13 comments, 👍3 — highest-engagement issue today.
  2. #10074 — Anthropic edit calls on Korean text silently corrupt non-ASCII arguments (dropped u in \uXXXX → control chars). Reproducible over three weeks; costs real retries. Closed today, 12 comments.
  3. #11021 — ChatGPT sign-in reports 272K context for gpt-6.1-sol while the account catalog advertises 500K, shrinking Pi's compaction budget. 10 comments, 👍8 — top-voted issue.
  4. #7062 — openai-completions mishandles array-typed delta.content (renders [object Object]) and missing finish_reason, breaking Databricks/Qwen/gpt-oss reasoning models. 9 comments, 👍3.
  5. #10812 — A saved default model removed from the catalog is silently ignored and falls back to another model with no warning. 7 comments.
  6. #11869 — New StringEnum in Pi 1.5.0 breaks compile-time typing (unknown params) because it no longer uses typebox. P0, 👍3.
  7. #11956 — Cancelling a read during file open crashes Pi with an uncaught AbortError. Closed today; fix PR #12025.
  8. #10536 — Cache warming never refreshes for sessions on virtual/extension-router models. Companion to #10956.
  9. #11989 — Anthropic OAuth pins claude-cli/2.1.280, rejected as too old for newer models (needs 2.1.290). Breaking subscription-based access.
  10. #12014 — Lone UTF-16 surrogates in tool-call arguments are not stripped, poisoning every subsequent request in the session.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #12025 — Fixes #11956: prevents crashes when an aborted signal destroys an unwatched file stream in the read tool.
  2. #11961 — pi-durable: Harness.close() now releases provider session resources, allowing processes to exit cleanly (fixes #11676).
  3. #11951 — Session index reworked as Chord outbox; sessions become authoritative with derived index/mirror.
  4. #12002 — Migrates the session catalog from standalone catalog.sqlite to host-keyed rows in the server's Chord store, enabling backup/export/import coherence.
  5. #12011 — Follow-up migration of shares and subagents tables into Chord stores.
  6. #11990 — Prototype Radius session sync adapter, giving p2 a backend boundary for backup/restore.
  7. #12016 — Adds Microsoft Entra ID (DefaultAzureCredential) auth for Azure OpenAI, enabling Foundry access without API keys.
  8. #11998 — Replaces deprecated Ling 2.6/Ring 2.6 with Ling 3.x Flash family (3.2 supports image input).
  9. #11986 — Tool search now ranks read-only tools for read-verb queries (e.g. "read my email" → gmail_read_email).
  10. #11985 — Codemode wrapper no longer shadows prelude globals (tools, console).

Also notable: a cluster of llama.cpp doc/port PRs (#12005, #12004, #12001, #11958, #11960) standardizes on llama serve and port 9931.

5. Hot Discussions

Ideas

  • #11984 — Proposal to use Redux/Redux-Saga effects for Pi state management, referencing an external redux-saga discussion. 👍1, 0 comments — early-stage.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • New provider integrations: Modal as a native inference provider (#12024), Microsoft Entra ID for Azure OpenAI (#12016, PR), expanded Cloudflare AI Gateway upstreams (#10539).
  • Provider/auth catalog fidelity: Aligning reported context windows and model pickers with live account catalogs (#11021, #10683), and OAuth host corrections (#9819).
  • Session/state continuity: Forking orphaned sessions (v1.5.2), Chord-backed session catalog and sync (#12002, #12011, #11951, #11990).
  • Extension ecosystem ergonomics: npm package resolution via main/exports (#9817), standalone binary dependency resolution (#12012), and config-tracking friendliness (#6415).
  • Tool-call robustness: Repairing malformed arguments (#11112), array content handling (#7062), surrogate stripping (#12014).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Cache warming reliability: Multiple independent reports (#10956, #10536) of idle warming silently disabling itself under extensions, virtual models, or context compaction — a recurring, hard-to-diagnose class of bug.
  • Silent failures and corruption: Anthropic non-ASCII/escape-sequence corruption (#10074), silent model fallbacks (#10812), and surrogate poisoning (#12014) all degrade trust because failures are invisible until damage is done.
  • Provider/model metadata drift: Context windows, OAuth version pins, and catalogs disagreeing with server state (#11021, #11989, #10683, #10539) cause confusing errors on otherwise valid setups.
  • Crash-on-cancel: Abort handling remains fragile (#11956), where cancellation paths produce uncaught exceptions — particularly painful in parallel codemode scripts.
  • Type-safety regressions in releases: StringEnum change (#11869) shows how internal refactors can break downstream extension compilation, underscoring a need for stricter semver discipline in pi-ai.

  • Web Shell intelligence & search: stateful intelligent UI (native components + isolated HTML visualization) (#14019), custom-provider model discovery with refresh-and-select (#16785), and a dedicated centered session-search dialog (#16778).
  • Unified agent loop: one core loop implementation shared across all surfaces behind experimental.unifiedAgentLoop (#15327).
  • GraphQL batching for the GitHub channel CI re-check leg (#16692).
  • Real bash parsing for safety attribution instead of a hand-rolled shell model (#16604).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • CI flakiness dominates triage bandwidth: the top of the updated-Issues list is nearly all qwen-code-dev-bot auto-files — #14724 (292 comments), #16672, #11680, and several deflake issues like #16863 and #16853.
  • Multi-agent reliability: permission approvals that never render (#16425), teammates never reaching the leader in ACP mode (#15738), and subagent context blow-up (#15660).
  • Session command deadlocks: /cd and /branch both fail with "response or tool call in progress" even when nothing is running (#12224, #16700).
  • Safety classifier blind spots: redirection placement hiding arguments (#16856) and the AUTO classifier being fed already-executed calls (#16496).
  • Rendering/terminal edge cases: word-wrap orphan characters in Static mode at full terminal width (#14075).

Note: The advisory link at the very top of the source data was truncated as [advisory](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/security/advisories/GHSA-mh. If this is a security advisory (GHSA-mh…), maintainers should follow up on the full URL — it did not match any Issue/PR in the provided dataset.
